4.8.1: That is the royal hero’s lofty nature: he, manifold, hath gained immortal powers. Stride forth to heaven’s broad regions, thou, a tiger on a tiger’s skin. Let all the people long for thee. Let heavenly floods be rich in milk.

4.10.1: Born in the heaven, sprung from the sea, brought to us hither from the flood. This gold-born Shell shall be to us an amulet to lengthen life.

4.16.1: A charm to secure freedom from various evils We seize and hold thee, Conquering One! the queen of medi- cines that heal. O Plant, I have endowed thee with a hundred powers for every man,
4.16.2: Still conquering, banishing the curse, mighty, with thy reverted. bloom. Thee and all Plants have I invoked: Hence let it save us! was my prayer.
4.16.3: She who hath cursed us with a curse, or hath conceived a murderous sin, Or seized our son to take his blood, may she devour the child she bare. What magic they have wrought for thee in dish unbaked or burnt dark-red,

4.16.5: All the she-fiends of evil name and voice, we drive away from us. Death caused by famine, caused by thirst, failure of children,. loss of kine, With thee, O Apāmārga, all this ill we cleanse and wipe away.
4.16.6: Death caused by thirst, death caused by stress of hunger, loss at play with dice, All this, O Apāmārga with thine aid we cleanse and wipe away.

4.17.2: Back to its author turn the spell like a dear damsel to her friend! I with this Plant have ruined all malignant powers of witchery. The spell which they have laid upon thy field, thy cattle, or thy men.
4.17.3: No power had he who wrought the spell: he hurt his foot, he broke his toe. His act hath brought us happiness and pain and sorrow to him- self.
4.17.4: Let Apāmārga sweep away chronic disease and every curse, Sweep sorceresses clean away, and all malignant stingy hags. Sweep thou away the sorcerers, all stingy fiendish hags away.
4.17.5: All this, O Apāmārga, with thine aid we wipe away from us. Thou breakest ties of kith and kin, thou causest, too, relation- ship:

4.18.1: As once when time began the Gods with thee expelled the Asuras,
4.18.2: Even thence, O Plant, wast thou produced as one who wipes and sweeps away. Thy father’s name was Cleaver. Thou with thousand branches cleavest all. Do thou, turned backward, cleave and rend the man who treateth us as foes.
4.18.3: The evil sprang from earth; it mounts to heaven and spreads to vast extent. Reverted, shaking him with might, thence on its maker let it fall.
4.18.4: For thou hast grown reverted, and turned backward also is thy fruit. Remove all curses far from me, keep most remote the stroke of death. Preserve me with a hundred, yea, protect me with a thousand aids.
4.18.5: May mighty Indra, Lord of Plants! give store of strength and. power to thee. A charm for the acquisition of superhuman powers of sight
4.18.6: It sees in front, it sees behind, it sees afar away, it sees The sky, the firmament, and earth: all this, O Goddess, it beholds. Through thee, O godlike Plant, may I behold all creatures that exist,
4.18.7: Three several heavens, three several earths, and these six regions one by one. The pupil, verily, art thou of that celestial Engle’s eye.
4.18.8: On earth hast thou alighted as a weary woman seeks her couch. The God who hath a thousand eyes give me this Plant in my right hand! I look on every one therewith, each Sūdra and each Āryan man.
4.19.1: Make manifest the forms of things; hide not their essences from sight. And, thou who hast a thousand eyes, look the Kimidins in the face.
4.19.2: Make me see Yātudhānas, make thou Yātudhānis visible. Make me see all Pisāchas With this prayer, O Plant, I hold thee fast. Thou art the sight of Kasyapa and of the hound who hath four eyes.
4.19.3: Make the Pisācha manifest as Sūrya when he rides at noon. Kimidin, Yātudhāna from their hiding-places have I dragged.
4.19.4: I look on every one with this, Sūdra and Aryan man alike. Make that Pisācha visible, the fiend who flies in middle air, The fiend who glides across the sky, and him who deems the earth his help.
4.19.5: Glorification and benediction of cows The kine have come and brought good fortune: let them rest in the cow-pen and be happy
4.19.6: near us. Here let them stay prolific, many-coloured, and yield through many morns their milk for Indra.
4.19.7: Indra aids him who offers sacrifice and praise: he takes not what is his, and gives him more thereto.
4.19.8: Increasing ever more and ever more his wealth, he makes the pious dwell within unbroken bounds. These are ne’er lost, no robber ever injures them: no evil-minded foe attempts to harass them.
4.20.1: The master of the kine lives a long life with these, the Cows whereby he pours his gifts and serves the Gods.
4.20.2: The charger with his dusty brow o’ertakes them not, and never to the shambles do they take 44 their way.
4.20.3: These Cows, the cattle of the pious worshipper, roam over wide- spread pasture where no danger is.
4.20.4: To me the Cows seem Bhaga, they seem Indra, they seem a portion of the first poured Soma. These present Cows, they, O ye men, are Indra. I long for Indra with my heart and spirit. O Cows, ye fatten e’en the worn and wasted, and make the unlovely beautiful to look on.
4.20.5: Prosper my home, ye with auspicious voices! Your power is magnified in our assemblies. In goodly pasturage, bright-hued, prolific, drinking pure water at fair drinking-places,

4.20.7: Exalt and strengthen this my Prince, O Indra, Make him sole lord and leader of the people. Scatter his foes, deliver all his rivals into his hand in struggles for precedence.
4.20.8: Give him a share in village, kine, and horses, and leave his enemy without a portion. Let him as King be head and chief of Princes, Give up to him, O Indra, every foeman.
4.20.9: Let him be treasure-lord of goodly treasures, let him as King be master of the people. Grant unto him great power and might, O Indra, and strip his enemy of strength and vigour.

4.21.7: So bear thou to the Gods the prayer we utter. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. I pray to Agni in each act successful, employed in every sacrifice, the strongest, Fiend-slayer, served with fatness, strengthening worship. May he deliver us from grief and
4.22.1: trouble. We invoke the oblation-bearer, well-born Agni Jātavedas,
4.22.2: Him, Vaisvānara, almighty. May he set us free from trouble. With whom as friend the Rishis gave their power new splendour, with whom they kept aloof the Asuras’ devices,
4.22.3: Agni, with whom Indra subdued the Panis. May he deliver us. from grief and trouble. Through whom the Gods discovered life eternal, through whom they stored the plants with
4.22.4: pleasant juices, Through whom they brought to men the light of heaven. May he deliver us from grief and 45
4.22.5: trouble. I, suppliant, praise and ever call on Agni, sole Lord of all this world, of all that shineth,
4.22.6: Of what exists and shall exist hereafter. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. A hymn of prayer and praise to Indra I think of Indra, only him for ever, fiend-slayer, May these lauds of mine come near him.
4.22.7: He cometh to the pious offerer’s calling. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. Who with strong arms o’ercame his strong opponents, who broke and crushed the power of
4.23.1: the demons, Who won the rivers and the kine in battle. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. Ruler of men, finder of light, the hero: the pressing-stones declare his valour, master.
4.23.2: Of sweetest sacrifice with seven Hotars. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. The lord of barren cows and bulls and oxen, finder of light for whom the posts are planted,
4.23.3: For whom the bright juice flows cleansed by devotion. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. Whose favour those desire who offer Soma, whom, arrow-bearer, men invoke in battle,
4.23.4: On whom the hymn depends, in whom is power, May he deliver us from grief and trouble. Why was born, first, for active operation, whose valour as the first hath been awakened,
4.23.5: Who raised his bolt when he encountered Ahi. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. Strong Lord, who leadeth hosts to meet for battle, who sendeth riches both of earth and heaven,
4.23.6: I, suppliant, praise and ever call on Indra. May he deliver us from grief and trouble. A hymn of prayer and praise to Vāyu and Savitar
4.23.7: I think on Vāyu’s and Savitar’s holy rites, ye twain who penetrate and guard the living world: Ye who have come to be this All’s pervaders, deliver us, ye two from grief and trouble. Ye who have counted up the earth’s expanses, and in the sky smoothed out the air’s mid region,
4.24.1: Whose going-forth hath ne’er been reached by any, deliver us, ye two, from grief and trouble. Beauteously bright! men rest in thy dominion when thou hast risen up and hastened onward.
4.24.2: Ye, Vāyu, Savitar, preserve all creatures. Deliver us, ye, twain, from grief and trouble. Hence, Vāyu, Savitar drive evil action, chase Simidā away, drive off the demons. Ye give us store of energy and power. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.24.3: Of their own selves let Savitar and Vāyu send favourable strength and wealth and plenty. Here give us perfect freedom from consumption. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.24.4: Ye, Savitar and Vāyu, to assist us, enjoy the hymn and the delightful cheerer. Come hither downward from the stream of blessing. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.24.5: Like noblest benisons they have stayed in the God loving man’s abode. I glorify bright Savitar and Vāyu. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.24.6: A hymn to Heaven and Earth O Heaven and Earth, I think on you, wise, givers of abundant gifts, ye who through measureless expanses have spread forth.
4.24.7: For ye are seats and homes of goodly treasures. Deliver us, ye twain from grief and trouble. Yea, seats and homes are ye of goodly treasures, grown strong, divine, blessed, and far 46
4.25.1: extending, To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. I call on you who warm and cause no sorrow, deep, spacious, meet to be adored by poets.
4.25.2: To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye who maintain Amrit and sacrifices, ye who support rivers and human beings,
4.25.3: To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye by whom cows and forest trees are cherished within whose range all creatures are included,
4.25.4: To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye who delight in nectar and in fatness, ye without whom men have no strength or power,
4.25.5: To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. The grief that pains me here, whoever caused it, not sent by fate, hath sprung from human action.
4.25.6: I, suppliant, praise Heaven, Earth, and oft invoke them. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.25.7: A hymn to the Maruts I think upon the Maruts: may they bless me, may they assist me to this wealth in battle. I call them like swift well-trained steeds to help us. May they deliver us from grief and
4.26.1: trouble. Those who surround the never-failing fountain for ever, and bedew the plants with moisture,
4.26.2: The Maruts, Prini’s sons, I chiefly honour. May they deliver us from grief and trouble. Bards, who invigorate the milk of milch-kine, the sap of growing plants, the speed of coursers To us may the strong Maruts be auspicious. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
4.26.3: They who raised water from the sea to heaven and send it from the sky to earth in showers, The Maruts who move mighty with their waters, may they deliver us from grief and trouble.
4.26.4: They who delight in nectar and in fatness, they who bestow upon us health and vigour. The Maruts who rain mighty with their waters, may they deliver us from grief and trouble. Whether with stormy might the Maruts established this All, or
4.26.5: Gods with their celestial power, Ye, kindly Gods, are able to restore it. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
4.26.6: Potent in battles is the Maruts’ army, impetuous train, well- known, exceeding mighty. I, suppliant, praise and oft invoke the Maruts. May they deliver us from grief and trouble. A hymn to Bhava and Sarva
4.26.7: I Reverence you—mark this—Bhava and Sarva, ye under whose control is this that shineth. Lords of this world both quadruped and biped. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.27.1: Lords of all near and even of what is distant, famed as the best and skilfullest of archers, Lords of this world both quadruped and biped, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Thousand-eyed foe-destroyers, I invoke you, still praising you the strong, of wide dominion:
4.27.2: Lords of this world both quadruped and biped, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye who of old wrought many a deed in concert, and showed among mankind unhappy
4.27.3: omens; Lords of this world both quadruped and biped, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye from the stroke of whose destroying weapon not one among the Gods or men escapeth,
4.27.4: Lords of this world both quadruped and biped, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Hurl your bolt, strong Gods, at the Yātudhāna, him who makes ready roots and deals in
4.27.5: 47 magic: Lords of this world both quadruped and biped, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.27.6: Comfort and aid us, ye strong Gods, in battles, at each Kimidin send your bolt of thunder. I, suppliant, praise and ever call on Bhav and Sarva. Set us free from grief and trouble.
4.27.7: A hymn to Mitra-Varuna You twain, O Mitra, Varuna, I honour, Lawstrengtheners, wise, who drive away oppressors. Ye who protect the truthful in his battles, deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
4.28.1: Ye the wise Gods who drive away oppressors, ye who protect the truthful in his battles, Who come, men’s guards, to juice pressed forth by Babhru,. deliver us, ye twain, from grief
4.28.2: and trouble. Mitra and Varuna who help Agasti, Atri, and Angiras, and Jamadagni,
4.28.3: Ye who help Kasyapa, who help Vasishtha, deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Mitra and Varuna, who help Syāvāsva, Atri, and Purumilha, and Vadhryasva,
4.28.4: Ye who help Vimada and Saptavadhri, deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye, Varuna, Mitra, who give aid to Kutsa, Gavishthira, Bharadvāja, Visvāmitra,
4.28.5: Who help Kakshivan and give aid to Kanva, deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Ye, Mitra, Varuna, who help Trisoka, Medhātithi, and Usanā son of Kavi,
4.28.6: Ye, Gotama’s and Mudgala’s protectors, deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble. Whose straight-reined car that keeps the track of goodness assails and ruins him who walks perversely
4.28.7: I, suppliant, praise with constant invocation Mitra and Varuna. Save us from affliction.
4.29.1: A glorification of vāk or speech I travel with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and All-Gods I wander.
4.29.2: I hold aloft both Varuna and Mitra, I hold aloft Indra and both the Asvins. I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit
4.29.3: worship. The Gods, making me enter many places, in diverse spots have set mine habitation. I, verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods, and men alike shall welcome.
4.29.4: I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Rishi, and a Brāhman.
4.29.5: Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them, each man who sees, breathes, hears, the word out-spoken. They know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it.
4.29.6: I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion. I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated
4.29.7: Earth and Heaven. I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvashtar I support, Pashan, and Bhaga.
4.30.1: I load with wealth the zealous sacrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation. On the world’s summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean.
4.30.2: Thence I extend o’er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead. 48 I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence.
4.30.3: Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur. A hymn to Manyu or Wrath
4.30.4: Borne on with thee, O Manyu girt by Maruts, let our brave men, impetuous, bursting forward, March on, like flames of fire in form, exulting, with pointed arrows, sharpening their weapons.
4.30.5: Flashing like fire, be thou, O conquering Manyu, invoked, O victor, as our army’s leader. Slay thou our foes, distribute their possession: show forth thy vigour, scatter those who hate
4.30.6: us. O Manyu, overcome those who assail us. On! breaking, slaying, crushing down the foemen. They have not hindered thine impetuous vigour: mighty! sole born! reduce them to
4.30.7: subjection. Alone of many thou art worshipped, Manyu: sharpen the spirit of each clan for combat.
4.30.8: With thee to aid, O thou of perfect splendour, we raise the glorious battle-shout for conquest. Unyielding, bringing victory like Indra, O Manyu be thou here our sovran ruler. To thy dear name. O victor, we sing praises: we know the spring from which thou art come
4.31.1: hither. Twin-borne with power, destructive bolt of thunder the highest conquering might is thine,
4.31.2: subduer! Be friendly to us in thy spirit, Manyu! O much-invoked, in shock of mighty battle! For spoil let Varuna and Manyu give us the wealth of both sides gathered and collected;
4.31.3: And let our enemies with stricken spirits, o’er-whelmed with. terror, sling away defeated. A hymn to Manyu
4.31.4: He who hath reverenced thee, Manyu, destructive bolt! breeds. for himself forthwith all conquering energy. Arya and Dāsa will we conquer with thine aid, with thee the conqueror, with conquest
4.31.5: conquest-sped. Manyu was Indra, yea, the God was Manyu; Manyu was Hotar
4.31.6: Varuna, Jātavedas. The tribes of human lineage worship Manyu. Accordant, with thy fervour, Manyu! guard us. Come hither, Manyu, mightier than the mighty: smite, with thy fervour, for ally, our foemen.
4.31.7: Slayer of foes, of Vritra, and of Dasyu, bring thou to us all kinds of wealth and treasure. For thou art, Manyu, of surpassing vigour, fierce, queller of the foe, and self-existent,
4.32.1: Shared by all men, victorious, subduer: vouchsafe to us superior strength in battles. I have departed still without a portion, wise God! according to thy will, the mighty. I, feeble man, was wroth with thee, O Manyu. Come in thy proper form and give us vigour.
4.32.2: Come hither, I am all thine own: advancing, turn thou to me, victorious, all-bestowing. Come to me, Manyu, wielder of the thunder: bethink thee of thy friend, and slay the Dasyus.
4.32.3: Approach, and on our right hand hold thy station, then let us slay a multitude of foemen. The best of meath I offer to support thee: may we be first to drink thereof in quiet. A prayer to Agni for protection and prosperity
4.32.4: Chasing our pain with splendid light, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us. His lustre flash our pain away.
4.32.5: 49 For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee. His lustre flash our pain away!
4.32.6: Best praiser of all these be he, and foremost be our noble chiefs. His lustre flash our pain away!
4.32.7: So that thy worshipper and we, thine, Agni! in our sons may live. His lustre flash our pain away! As ever conquering Agni’s beams of splendour go to every side,
4.33.1: His lustre flash our pain away. To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere.
4.33.2: His lustre flash our pain away! O thou whose face looks every way, bear off our foes as in a ship. His lustre flash our pain away!
4.33.3: As in a ship across the flood, transport us to felicity. His lustre flash our pain away Glorification of the Vishtāri sacrifice
4.33.4: The head of this is prayer, its back the Brihat, Odanas’s belly is the Vāmadevya; Its face reality, its sides the metre, Vishtāri sacrifice produced from fervour. Boneless, cleansed, purified by him who cleanseth, they go res- plendent to the world of
4.33.5: splendour. Fire burneth not their organ of enjoyment: much pleasure have they in the world of Svarga.
4.33.6: Never doth want or evil fortune visit those who prepare oblation called Vishtāri. He goes unto the Gods, he dwells with Yama, he joys among Gandharvas meet for Soma.
4.33.7: Yama robs not of generative vigour the men who dress oblation called Vishtāri. Borne on his car, a charioteer, he travels: endowed with wings he soars beyond the heavens.
4.33.8: Strongest is this, performed, of sacrifices: he hath reached heaven who hath prepared Vishtāri. The oval-fruited lotus spreads his fibre: there bloom the nelo- phar and water-lilies.
4.34.1: Abundant with their overflow of sweetness, these streams shall reach thee in the world of Svarga, whole lakes with lotus- blossom shall approach thee.
4.34.2: Full lakes of butter with their banks of honey, flowing with wine, and milk and curds and water Abundant with their overflow of sweetness, these streams shall reach thee in the world of
4.34.3: Svarga, whole lakes with lotus- blossom shall approach thee. I give four pitchers, in four several places, filled to the brim with milk and curds and water.
4.34.4: Abundant with their overflow of sweetness, these streams shall reach thee in the world of Svarga, whole lakes with lotus- blossom shall approach thee. I part this Odana among the Brāhmans, Vishtāri, conquering worlds and reaching heaven.
4.34.5: Let me not lose it: swelling by its nature, be it my perfect Cow to grant all wishes! Magnification of the Odana or oblation of milk and rice
4.34.6: Odana which Prajāpati, the firstborn of Order, dressed with fervour for the Brāhman, which guards the worlds from breaking atIthe centre,—I with this Odana will conquer Mrityu.
4.34.7: Whereby the World-Creators vanquished Mrityu, that which they found by fervour, toil and trouble,
4.34.8: That which prayer first made ready for the Brāhman,—I with this Odana will conquer Mrityu. 50 That which upholds the Earth, the all-sustainer, that which hath filled air’s middle realm with
4.35.1: moisture, Which, raised on high in grandeur, stablished heaven,—I with this Odana will conquer
4.35.2: Mrityu. From which the months with thirty spokes were moulded, from which the twelve-spoked year was formed and fashioned.
4.35.3: Which circling day and night have ne’er o’ertaken,—I with this Odana will conquer Mrityu.
4.35.4: Which hath become breath-giver, life-bestower; to which the worlds flow full of oil and fatness, To whom belong all the refulgent regions,—I with this Odana will conquer Mrityu.
4.35.5: From which, matured, sprang Amrit into being, which hath become Gāyatris lord and ruler, In which the perfect Vedas have been treasured,—I with this
4.35.6: Odana will conquer Mrityu, I drive away the hostile God-despiser: far off be those who are mine adversaries, I dress Brahmaudana that winneth all things. May the Gods hear me who believe and trust
4.35.7: them. A charm against fiends, human enemies, and other pests
4.36.1: Endowed with true strength, let the Bull, Agni Vaisvānara, burn them up. Him who would pain and injure us, him who would treat us as a foe. Him who, unharmed, would injure us, and him who, harmed, would do us harm,
4.36.10: I lay between the doubled fangs of Agni, of Vaisvānara. Those who, what time the moon is dark, hunt with loud cry and answering shout,
4.36.2: Flesh-eaters, others who would harm,—all these I overcome with might. I conquer the Pisāchas with my power, and take their wealth away. All who would injure us I slay. Let mine intention have success.
4.36.3: With Gods who flee with him, and match their rapid motion with the Sun, I with those animals who dwell in rivers and on hills am found.
4.36.4: I trouble the Pisāchas as the tiger plagues men rich in kine. They, even as dogs when they have seen a lion, find no hiding- place. Naught with Pisāchas can I do, with thieves, with roamers of the wood.
4.36.5: Pisāchas flee and vanish from each village as I enter it. Into whatever village this mine awful power penetrates,
4.36.6: Thence the Pisāchas flee away, and plot no further mischief there. Those who enrage me with their prate, as flies torment an elephant, I deem unhappy creatures, like small insects troublesome to man.
4.36.7: Destruction seize upon the man, as with a cord they hold a horse, The fool who is enraged with me! He is not rescued from the noose.
4.36.8: A charm against Gandharvas and Apsarases With thee, O Plant, in olden time Atharvans smote and slew the fiends. Kasyapa smote with thee, with thee did Kanava and Agastya smite.
4.36.9: With thee we scare and drive away Gandharvas and Apsarases. O Ajasringi, chase the fiends. Cause all to vanish with thy smell.
4.37.1: Let the Apsarases, puffed away, go to the river, to the ford,— Guggulū, Pīlā, Naladi, Aukshagandhi, Pramandini. 51
4.37.10: Ye have become attentive since the Apsarases have past away. Where great trees are, Asvatthas and Nyagrodhas with their leafy crests,
4.37.11: There where your swings are green and bright, and lutes and cymbals sound in tune, ‘Ye have become attentive since the Apsarases have past away. Hither hath come this one, the most effectual of herbs and plants.
4.37.12: Let Ajasringi penetrate, Arāaki with sharpened horn. From the Gandharva, dancing near, the lord of the Apsarases,
4.37.2: Wearing the tuft of hair, I take all manhood and virility. With those dread hundred iron spears, the darts of Indra, let it pierce. The Blyxa-fed Gandharvas, those who bring no sacrificial gift.
4.37.3: With those dread hundred golden spears, the darts of Indra, let it pierce. The Blyxa-fed Gandharvas, those who bring no sacrificial gift.
4.37.4: O Plant, be thou victorious, crush the Pisāchas, one and all, Blyxa-fed, shining in the floods, illumining the selfish ones. Youthful, completely decked with hair, one monkey-like, one like a dog,—
4.37.5: So the Gandharva, putting on a lovely look, pursues a dame. Him with an efficacious charm we scare and cause to vanish hence.
4.37.6: Your wives are the Apsarases, and ye, Gandharvas, are their lords. Run ye, immortal ones, away: forbear to interfere with men! A charm for success in gambling
4.37.7: Hither I call the Apsaras, victorious, who plays with skill, Her who comes freely fort to view, who wins the stakes in games of dice.
4.37.8: Hither I call that Apsaras who scatters and who gathers up. The Apsaras who plays with skill and takes her winnings in the game. Dancing around us with the dice, winning the wager by her play.
4.37.9: May she obtain the stake for us and gain the victory with skill. May she approach us full of strength: let them not win this wealth of ours.
4.38.1: Hither I call that Apsaras, the joyous, the delightful one— Those nymphs who revel in the dice, who suffer grief and yield to wrath. Who follow in their course the rays of Sūrya, or as a particle of light attend him.
4.38.2: Whose leader from afar, with store of riches, compasses quickly all the worlds and guards them.
4.38.3: Pleased, may he come to this our burnt oblation, together with the Air, enriched with treasure. Together with the Air, O rich in treasure, guard here the white cow and the calf, O mighty! Here are abundant drops for thee, come hither! Here is thy white calf, let thy mind be with us.
4.38.4: Together with the Air, O rich in treasure, keep the white calf in safety here, O mighty! Here is the grass, here is the stall, here do we bind the calf. We are your masters, name by
4.38.5: name. All Hail! A prayer to various deities for health, wealth, and prosperity Agni no earth kath had mine homage. May he bless me.
4.38.6: As I have bowed me down to Agni on the earth, so let the Favouring Graces bow them down to me.
4.38.7: Earth is the Cow, her calf is Agni. May she with her calf Agni yield me food, strength, all my wish, life first of all, and off- spring, plenty, wealth. All Hail! Vāyu in air hath had mine homage. May he bless me.
4.39.1: 52 As I have bowed me down to Vāyu in the air, so let the Favour- ing Graces bow them down
4.39.10: to me. Air is the Cow, her calf is Vāyu. May she with her calf Vāyu yield me food, strength, all my wish, life first of all, and off- spring, plenty, wealth. All Hail!
4.39.2: The Sun in heaven hath had my homage. May he bless me. As I have bowed me down unto the Sun in heaven, so let the
4.39.3: Favouring Graces bow them down to me. Heaven is the Cow, her calf Āditya. May she yield with her calf the Sun food, strength, and all my wish, life first of all, and offspring, plenty, wealth. All Hail!
4.39.4: To Chandra in the quarters have I bowed me. May he bless me. As unto Chandra in the quarters I have bent, so let the Favour- ing Graces bow them down to
4.39.5: me. The quarters are the Cows, their calf is Chandra. May they yield with their calf the Moon food, strength and all my wish, life first of all, and offspring, plenty, wealth. All Hail!
4.39.6: Agni moves having entered into Agni, the Rishis’ son, who guards from imprecations, I offer unto thee with reverent worship. Let me not mar the
4.39.7: Gods’ appointed service. Skilled in all ways, O God, O Jātavedas, I offer what is cleansed by heart and spirit. To all thy seven mouths, O Jātavedas. Do thou accept with pleasure my libation.
4.39.8: A charm against rival worshippers O Jātavedas, eastward sacrificers, as foes assail us from the eastern quarter.
4.39.9: May they, turned back, be pained for harming Agni. I drive them backward with mine incantation. O Jātavedas, southward sacrificers as foes assail us from the southern quarter.
4.40.1: May they, turned back, be pained for harming Yama. I smite them backward with mine incantation.
4.40.2: O Jātavedas, westward sacrificers as foes assail us from the western quarter. For harming Varuna be they turned and troubled! I smite them backward with mine incantation.
4.40.3: Jātavedas, northward sacrificers as foes assail us from the northern quarter. For harming Soma be they turned and troubled! I smite them backward with mine
4.40.4: incantation. O Jātavedas, nether sacrificers, as foes assail us from the stead- fast quarter. For harming Earth let them be turned and troubled. I smite them backward with mine
4.40.5: incantation. Those who pay sacrifice, O Jātavedas, from air assail us from the midway quarter.
4.40.6: For harming Vāyu be they turned and troubled! I smite them backward with mine incantation. The sacrificers from above assail us, O Jātavedas, from the lofty quarter. For wronging Sūrya be they turned and troubled! I smite them backward with mine
4.40.7: incantation. Those from all points assail us, Jātavedas, who sacrifice from intermediate regions.
4.40.8: For wronging Prayer let them be turned and troubled, I smite them backward with mine incantation. 53

5.1.1: A glorification of Trita and Varuna He who with special plans and deathless spirit, waxing, well- born, hath come unto his birth place,
5.1.2: As he who shines upholds the days, thus Trita, of pure life, bears the Three as their supporter. He who, the first, approached the holy statutes makes, after, many beauteous forms and
5.1.3: figures. Eager to drink, his birth-place first he entered who understands the word when yet unspoken.
5.1.4: He who—the fluid gold, with radiant kinsmen—to fervent glow delivered up thy body, On him both set names, that shall live for ever: to him the regions shall send robes to clothe
5.1.5: him, As these have gone to their primeval station, each gaining an imperishable dwelling,
5.1.6: May kissing mothers of the bards’ beloved bring the pole-draw- ing husband to the sister. By holy wisdom I a sage, Far-Strider! offer to thee this lofty adoration.
5.1.7: This worship both the mighty eddying rivers, coming together to this station, heighten. Seven are the pathways which the wise have fashioned: to one of these may come the
5.1.8: troubled mortal. On sure ground where the ways are parted standeth Life’s Pillar in the dwelling of the
5.1.9: Highest. Working, I go my way with deathless spirit: life, spirit, bodies have gone gladly thither.
5.2.1: Aye, Sakra also gives his gift of treasure as when the sacrificer meets with power. Yea, the son asks dominion of his father: this they declared the noblest path to welfare.
5.2.2: Varuna, let them see thy revelations: display the wondrous shapes of times to follow. Halt with the milk, its other half, thou minglest and with that half, strong! unbeguiled!
5.2.3: increasest. Let us exalt the gracious friend, the mighty, Varuna son of-Aditi, strength-giver.
5.2.4: We have told him the marvels sung by poets. The utterance of Heaven and Earth is truthful. A glorification of Indra
5.2.5: In all the worlds That was the best and highest whence sprang the Mighty One of splendid valour.
