6.110.1: Let not this one, O Agni, wound the highest of these: preserve thou him from utter ruin. Knowing the way do thou untie the nooses of the she-fiend: let all the Gods approve thee. Rend thou the; bonds of these asunder, Agni! the, threefold noose whereby the three were
6.110.2: fastened. Knowing the way untie the she-fiend’s nooses: free all, the son, the father, and the mother.
6.110.3: The elder brother’s bonds, still left unwedded, fettered in every limb and bound securely, Loose these, for they are bonds for loosing: Pūshan, turn woes away upon the babe-destroyer. A charm to banish the fiend Grāhi
6.111.1: This sin the Gods wiped off and laid on Trita, and Trita wiped it off on human beings. Thence if the female fiend hath made thee captive, the Gods by prayer shall banish her and
6.111.2: free thee. Enter the particles of light and vapours, go to the rising fogs or mists, O Evil! Hence! vanish in the foams of rivers. Pūshan, wipe woes away upon the babe-destroyer!
6.111.3: Stored in twelve separate places lies what Trita hath wiped away, the sins of human beings. Thence if the female fiend hath made thee captive, the Gods by prayer shall banish her and
6.111.4: free thee. A prayer for pardon of faults and errors in sacrificing Whatever God-provoking wrong we priests have done, O
6.112.2: Therefrom do ye deliver us, Ādityas! by the right of Law. Here set us free, O holy ones, Ādityas, by the right of Law. When striving, bringing sacrifice, we failed to offer it aright.
6.112.3: With ladle full of fatness we, worshippers, pouring holy oil, Striving, have failed, O all ye Gods, against our will, to offer it.
6.113.1: A prayer for forgiveness of sins Whatever wrong we wittingly or in our ignorance have done, Do ye deliver us therefrom, O all ye Gods, of one accord.
6.113.2: If I, a sinner, when awake or sleeping have committed sin, Free me therefrom as from a stake, from present and from future guilt.
6.113.3: As one unfastened from a stake, or cleansed by bathing after toil, As butter which the sieve hath cleansed, so all shall purge me from the sin. A prayer for pardon of sin against mother, father, son, or brother
6.114.1: The wealth which husbandmen aforetime, digging, like men who find their food with knowledge, buried,
6.114.2: This to the King, Vivasvān’s son, I offer, Sweet be our food and fit for sacrificing! May he, Vaivasvata, prepare our portion; May he whose share is mead with mead besprinkle. Our sin in hasty mood against our mother, or guilt whereby a sire is wronged and angered.
6.114.3: Whether this sin into our heart hath entered regarding mother, father, son or brother, Auspicious be to us the zeal and spirit of all the fathers who are here among us.
6.115.1: A prayer for freedom from debt That which I eat, a debt which still is owing, the tribute due to Yama, which supports me, p. a255
6.115.2: Thereby may I be free from debt, O Agni. Thou knowest how to rend all bonds asunder. Still dwelling here we give again this present; we send it forth, the living from the living.
6.115.3: Throwing away the grain whence I have eaten, thereby shall I be free from debt, O Agni. May we be free in this world and that yonder, in the third world may we be unindebted. May we, debt-free, abide in all the pathways, in all the worlds which Gods and Fathers visit.
6.116.1: A prayer for pardon of cheating at play If we have sinned with both our hands, desiring to take the host of dice for our possession,
6.116.2: May both Apsarases to-day forgive us that debt, the fiercely- conquering, fiercely-looking. Stern viewers of their sins who rule the people, forgive us what hash happened as we gambled.
6.116.3: Not urging us to pay the debt we owed him, he with a cord hath gone to Yama’s kingdom. My creditor, the man whose wife I visit, he, Gods! whom I approach with supplication,
6.117.1: Let not these men dominate me in speaking. Mind this, ye two Apsarases, Gods’ Consorts! A prayer for release from debts incurred without intention of payment
6.117.2: 95 The debt which I incur, not gaming, Agni! and, not intending to repay, acknowledge, p. a256
6.117.3: That may Vaisvānara, the best, our sovran, carry away into the world of virtue. I cause Vaisvānara to know, confessing the debt whose payment to the Gods is promised. He knows to tear asunder all these nooses: so may we dwell with him the gentle-minded.
6.118.1: Vaisvānara the Purifier purge me when I oppose their hope and break my promise, Unknowing in my heart. With supplication, whatever guilt there is in that, I banish.
6.118.2: A prayer for pardon of sins and felicity hereafter If we have injured Air, or Earth, or Heaven, if we have wronged our Mother or our Father, May Agni Gārhapatya here absolve us, and bear us up into the world of virtue.
6.118.3: Earth is our Mother, Aditi our birth-place: our brother Air save us from imprecation! Dyaus, Father, save us, from the world of Fathers! My world not lost, may I approach my
6.119.1: kindred. There where our virtuous friends, who left behind them their bodily infirmities, are happy, Free from distortion of the limbs and lameness, may we behold, in heaven, our sons and
6.119.2: parents. A prayer for happiness in heaven
6.119.3: Spreading them out, untie the snares that hold us, Varuna’s bonds, the upper and the lower. Drive from us evil dream, drive off misfortune; then let us go in- to the world of virtue. If thou art bound with cord or tied to timber, fixt in the earth, or by a word imprisoned,
6.120.1: Our Agni Gārhapatya here shall free thee, and lead thee up into the world of virtue. The two auspicious stars whose name is called Releasers have gone up.
6.120.2: Send Amrit hither, let it come freeing the captive from his bonds! Open thyself, make room: from bonds thou shalt release the prisoner. Freed, like an infant newly born, dwell in all pathways where thou wilt.
6.120.3: A prayer for happiness in heaven This portion I who understand deliver to Visvakarman first-born son of Order.
6.121.1: So may we follow to the end, unbroken, beyond old age, the thread which we have given. This long-drawn thread some follow who have offered in order- ed course oblation to the Fathers:
6.121.2: Some, offering and giving to the friendless, if they can give: herein they find their heaven. 3, Stand on my side and range yourselves in order, ye two! The faithful reach this world of
6.121.3: Svarga. p. a258 When your dressed food hath been bestowed on Agni, to guard it, wife and husband, come together!
6.121.4: Dwelling with zeal I mount in spirit after the lofty sacrifice as it departeth. Agni, may we, beyond decay, invited, in the third heaven, feast and enjoy the banquet.
6.122.1: These women here, cleansed, purified, and holy, I place at rest singly, in hands of Brāhmans. May Indra, Marut-girt, grant me the blessing I long for as I pour you this libation. A prayer for happiness in heaven
6.122.2: Ye who are present, unto you I offer this treasure brought to us by Jātavedas Happily will the sacrificer follow: do ye acknowledge him in highest heaven.
6.122.3: 96 Do ye acknowledge him in highest heaven: ye know the world here present in assembly. In peace will he who sacrifices follow: show him the joy which comes from pious actions.
6.122.4: Gods are the Fathers, and the Fathers Gods. I am the very man I am.
6.122.5: I cook, I give, I offer up oblation. From what I gave let me not be disparted. O King, take thou thy stand in heaven, there also let that gift be placed. p. a259 Recognize, King, the gift which we have given, and be gracious,
6.123.1: God! An Omen from the sky
6.123.2: From the high firmament, yea, out of heaven a water-drop with dew on me hath fallen. I, Agni! share the merit of the pious, with vigour, milk, and hymns and sacrifices. If from a tree that fruit hath fallen downward if, aught from air that is vāyu.
6.123.3: Where it hath touched my body or my garment, thence may the Waters drive Destruction backward.
6.123.4: It is a fragrant ointment, happy fortune, sheen all of gold, yea, purified from blemish. Spread over us are all purifications. Death and Malignity shall not subdue us. Glorification of a war-chariot
6.123.5: Mayst thou, O Tree, be firm indeed in body, our friend that furthers us, a goodly hero. Put forth thy strength, compact with thongs of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of
6.124.1: battle. Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood.
6.124.2: Honour with sacrifice the Car like Indra’s bolt, the Car girt round with straps, the vigour of the floods.
6.124.3: Thou bolt of Indra, vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuna and child of Mitra, As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O godlike
6.125.1: Chariot, these oblations. Glorification of the war drum
6.125.2: Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee. O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.
6.125.3: Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour, yea, thunder forth and drive away misfortunes. Drive hence, O Drum, drive thou away mischances. Thou art the fist of Indra, show thy
6.126.1: firmness. Conquer those yonder and let these be victors. Let the Drum speak aloud as battle’s signal. Let our men, winged with horses, fly together. Let our car- warriors, Indra! be triumphant.
6.126.2: A charm to banish various diseases Of abscess, of decline, of inflammation of the eyes. O Plant,
6.126.3: Of penetrating pain, thou Herb, let not a particle remain. Those nerves of thine, Consumption! which stand closely hidden in thy groin 97
6.127.1: I know the balm for that disease: the magic cure is Sipudru. We draw from thee piercing pain that penetrates and racks thy limbs,
6.127.2: That pierces ears, that pierces eyes, the abscess, and the heart’s disease. Downward and far away from thee we banish that unknown. decline. A charm for fair weather
6.127.3: What time the heavenly bodies chose the Weather Prophet as their King, They brought him favouring weather, and, Let this be his do- main, they said.
6.128.1: May we have weather fair at noon, May we have weather fair at eve, Fair weather when the morning breaks, fair weather when the night is come. Fair weather to the day and night, and to the stars and sun and moon.
6.128.2: Give favourable weather thou, King, Weather Prophet, unto us. Be worship ever paid to thee, O Weather Prophet, King of
6.128.3: Star s, Who gavest us oo weather in the evening and by night and day! A charm for success and happiness
6.128.4: With fortune of the Sisu tree—with Indra as my friend to aid I give myself a happy fate. Fly and begone, Malignities!
6.129.1: That splendour and felicity wherewith thou hast excelled the trees Give me therewith a happy fate. Fly and begone, Malignities Blind fortune, with reverted leaves that is deposited in trees—
6.129.2: Give me therewith a happy fate. Fly and begone, Malignities. A woman’s love-charm
6.129.3: This is the Apsarases’ love-spell, the conquering, resistless ones’. Send the spell forth, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me. I pray, may he remember me, think of me, loving and beloved.
6.130.1: Send forth the spell, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me. That he may think of me, that I may never, never think of him,.
6.130.2: Send forth the spell, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me. Madden him, Maruts, madden him. Madden him, madden him, O Air.
6.130.3: Madden him, Agni, madden him. Let him consume with love of me. A woman’s love-charm
6.130.4: Down upon thee, from head to foot, I draw the pangs of long- ing love. Send forth the charm, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me. Assent to this, O Heavenly Grace! Celestial Purpose, guide it well!
6.131.1: Send forth the charm, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me. If thou shouldst run three leagues away, five leagues, a horse’s daily stage,
6.131.2: Thence thou shalt come to me again and be the father of our sons. The same 98
6.131.3: The Philter, burning with the pangs of yearning love, which Gods have poured within the bosom of the floods,
6.132.1: That spell for thee I heat by Varuna’s decree. The charm which, burning with the pangs of love, the General Gods have poured within the bosom of the floods,
6.132.2: That spell for thee I heat by Varuna’s decree. The Philter, burning with the pangs of longing, which Indrāni hath effused within the waters’
6.132.3: depth, That spell for thee I heat by Varuna’s decree. The charm, aglow with longing, which Indra and Agni have effused within the bosom of the
6.132.4: floods, That spell for thee I heat by Varuna’s decree.
6.132.5: The charm aglow with longing which Mitra and Varuna have poured within the bosom of the floods, That spell for thee I heat by Varuna’s decree.
6.133.1: A glorification of the sacred girdle By the direction of that God we journey, he will seek means to save and he will free us;
6.133.2: The God who hath engirt us with this Girdle, he who hath fast- ened it, and made us ready. Thou, weapon of the Rishis, art adored and served with sacrifice. First tasting of the votive milk, Zone, be a hero-slayer thou!
6.133.3: As I am now Death’s Brahmachāri claiming out of the living world a man for Yama, So with Austerity and Prayer and Fervour I bind this Girdle round the man before me.
6.133.4: She hath become, Faith’s daughter, sprung from Fervour, the sister of the world-creating Rishis; As such, O Girdle, give us thought and wisdom, give us religious zeal and mental vigour.
6.133.5: Thou whom primeval Rishis girt about them, they who made the world, As such do thou encircle me, O Girdle, for long days of life.
6.134.1: A priest’s prayer for power to punish wrong-doers This Thunderbolt shall take its fill of Order, scare life away and overthrow the kingdom. Tear necks in pieces. rend napes asunder, even as the Lord of
6.134.2: Might the neck of Vritra. Down, down beneath the conquerors, let him not rise, concealed in earth, but lie down smitten with the bolt.
6.134.3: Seek out the fierce oppressor, yea, strike only the oppressor dead. p. a265 Down on the fierce oppressor’s head strike at full length, O Thunderbolt!
6.135.1: A priest’s fulmination against an enemy Whate’er I eat I turn to strength, and thus I grasp the Thunder- bolt,
6.135.2: Rending the shoulders of that man as Indra shattered Vritra’s neck. I drink together what I drink, even as the sea that swallows all. Drinking the life-breath of that man, we drink that man and swallow him.
6.135.3: Whate’er I eat I swallow up, even as the sea that swallows all. Swallowing that man’s vital breath, we swallow him completely up.
6.136.1: 99 A charm to promote the growth of hair Born from the bosom of wide Earth the Goddess, godlike Plant, art thou:
6.136.2: So we, Nitatnī! dig thee up to strengthen and fix fast the hair. Make the old firm, make new hair spring, lengthen what has already grown.
6.136.3: Thy hair where it is falling off, and with the roots is torn away, I wet and sprinkle with the Plant, the remedy for all disease. A charm to promote the growth of hair
6.137.1: The Plant which Jamadagni dug to make his daughter’s locks. grow long, This same hath Vitahavya brought to us from Asita’s abode.
6.137.2: They might be measured with a rein, meted with both extended arms. Let the black locks spring thick and strong and grow like reeds upon thy head. Strengthen the roots, prolong the points, lengthen the middle part, O Plant.
6.137.3: Let the black locks spring thick and strong and grow like reeds upon thy head. A woman’s imprecation on her unfaithful lover
6.138.1: O Plant, thy fame is spread abroad as best of all the herbs that grow. Unman for me to-day this man that he may wear the horn of hair. Make him a eunuch with a horn, set thou the crest upon his- head.
6.138.2: Let Indra with two pressing-stones deprive him of his manly strength. I have unmanned thee, eunuch! yea, impotent! made thee- impotent, and robbed thee,
6.138.3: weakling! of thy strength. Upon his head we set the horn, we set the branching ornament. Duas tuas venas, a Diis factas, in quibus stat vigor virilis, paxillo ligneo in testiculis ob istam
6.138.4: mulierem tibi findo. Ut mulieres mattam (tegetem) facturae arundinem lapide findunt, sic fascinum tuum cum
6.138.5: testiculis ob istam mulierem findo. A woman’s love-charm Thou hast grown up, a source of joy to bless me with pros- perity.
6.139.1: A hundred are thy tendrils, three-and-thirty thy descending shoots. With this that bears a thousand leaves I dry thy heart and wither it.
6.139.2: Let thy heart wither for my love and let thy month be dry for me. Parch and dry up with longing, go with lips that love of me hath dried. Drive us together, tawny! fair! a go-between who wakens love.
6.139.3: Drive us together, him and me, and give us both one heart and mind. Even as his mouth is parched who finds no water for his burn- ing thirst,
6.139.4: So parch and burn with longing, go with lips that love of me hath dried. Even as the Mungoose bites and rends and then restores the wounded snake, So do thou, Mighty one, restore the fracture of our severed love.
6.139.5: A blessing on a child’s first two teeth 100
6.140.1: Two tigers have grown up who long to eat the mother and the sire: Soothe, Brāhmanaspati, and thou, O Jātavedas, both these teeth. Let rice and barley be your food, eat also beans and sesamum.
6.140.2: This is the share allotted you, to be your portion, ye two Teeth. Harm not your mother and your sire.
6.140.3: Both fellow teeth have been invoked, gentle and bringing happi- ness. Else whither let the fierceness of your nature turn away, O Teeth! Harm not your mother or your sire.
6.141.1: A blessing on cattle Vayu collected these: to find their sustenance be Tvashtar’s care:
6.141.2: May Indra bless and comfort them, and Rudra look that they increase. Take thou the iron axe and make a pair by marks upon their ears. This sign the Asvins have impressed: let these increase and multiply.
6.141.3: Even as Gods and Asuras, even as mortal men have done, Do ye, that these may multiply in thousands, Asvins! make the mark.
6.142.1: A blessing on cattle Spring high, O Barley, and become much through thine own magnificence: p. a269 Burst all the vessels; let the bolt from heaven forbear to strike thee down.
6.142.2: As we invite and call to thee, Barley, a God who heareth us, Raise thyself up like heaven on high and be exhaustless as the sea.
6.142.3: Exhaustless let thine out-turns be, exhaustless be thy gathered heaps, Exhaustless be thy givers, and exhaustless those who eat of thee. 101

7.1.1: Glorification of the power of prayer and to Agni They who by thought have guided all that Speech hath best, or they who with their heart have uttered words of truth,
7.1.2: Made stronger by the strength which the third prayer bestows, have by the fourth prayer learned the nature of the Cow. Well knows this son his sire, he knows his mother well: he hath been son, and he hath been
7.2.1: illiberal. He hath encompassed heaven, and air’s mid-realm, and sky; he hath become this All; he hath come nigh to us.
7.3.1: Praise of Atharvan Invoke for us, proclaim in sundry places, the kinsman of the Gods, our sire Atharvan,
7.4.1: His mother’s germ, his father’s breath, the youthful, who with his mind hath noticed this oblation. To Vāyu God of the Wind
7.5.1: With thine eleven teams, to aid our wishes, yea, with thy two- and-twenty teams, O Vāyu, With all thy three-and-thirty teams for drawing, here loose these teams, thou who art prompt to listen!
7.5.2: A glorification of sacrifice The Gods adored the Sacrifice with worship: these were the statutes of primeval ages. Those mighty ones attained the cope of heaven, there where the
7.5.3: Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling. Sacrifice was, was manifest among us: it sprang to life and then in time grew stronger. Then it became thedeities’ lord and ruler: may it bestow on us abundant riches.
7.5.4: Where the Gods worshipped Gods with their oblation, worship- ped immortals with immortal spirit, p. a272 There in the loftiest heaven may we be happy, and look upon that light when Sūrya rises.
7.5.5: With their oblation, Purusha, the Gods performed a sacrifice. A sacrifice more potent still they paid with the invoking hymn. With dog the Gods, perplexed, have paid oblation, and with cow’s limbs in sundry sacrifices.
7.6.1: Invoke for us, in many a place declare him who with his mind. hath noticed this our worship. A prayer to Aditi for help and protection Aditi is sky, and air’s mid-region, Aditi is the father, son, and mother,
7.6.2: Aditi all the Gods and the Five Nations, Aditi what is now and what is future. We call for help the Queen of Law and Order, great mother of all those whose ways are 102
7.6.3: righteous, Far-spread, unwasting strong in her dominion, Aditi wisely lead- ing, well protecting. Sinless may we ascend, for weal, the vessel, rowed with good oars, divine, that never leaketh,
7.6.4: Earth, our strong guard, incomparable Heaven, Aditi wisely lead- ing, well protecting. Let us bring hither, in pursuit of riches, Aditi with our word, the mighty mother, Her in whose lap the spacious air is lying: may she afford us triply-guarding shelter!
7.7.1: Praise of the Ādityas I have sung praise to Diti’s sons and Aditi’s, those very lofty and invulnerable Gods. For far within the depths of ocean is their home and in the wor- ship paid them none excelleth
7.8.1: these. Godspeed to a departing traveller Go forward on thy way from good to better: Brihaspati pre- cede thy steps and guide thee!
7.9.1: Place this man here, within this earth’s enclosure, afar from foes with all his men about him. A prayer to Pūshan for protection and the recovery of lost property Pūshan was born to move on distant pathways, on roads remote from earth, remote from
7.9.2: heaven. To both most lovely places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge. Pūshan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and
7.9.3: danger. Giver of blessings, glowing, all heroic, may he the wise and watchful go before us. We are thy praisers here, O Pūshan: never let us be injured under thy protection.
7.9.4: From out the distance, far and wide, may Pūshan stretch his right hand forth. Let him drive back our lost to us, let us return with what is lost. A prayer for the favour of Sarasvati
7.10.1: That breast of thine, exhaustless and delightful, good to invoke, beneficent, free giver. Wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest, bring that, Sarasvati, that we may drain it.
7.11.1: A prayer to protect corn from lightning and drought That far-spread thunder, sent from thee, which cometh on all this world, a high celestial signal
7.12.1: Strike not, O God, our growing corn with lightning, not kill it with the burning rays of Sūrya. A prayer for influence at deliberative and religious meetings In concord may Prajapati’s two daughters, Gathering and As- sembly, both protect me.
7.12.2: May every man I meet respect and aid me. Fair be my words, O Fathers, at the meetings. We know thy name, O Conference: thy name is interchange of talk.
7.12.3: 103 Let all the company who join the Conference agree with me. Of these men seated here I make the splendour and the lore mine own.
7.12.4: Indra, make me conspicuous in all this gathered company. Whether your thoughts are turned away, or bound and fastened here or there, We draw them hitherward again: let your mind firmly rest on me.
7.13.1: A charm to win superiority over foes and rivals As the Sun, rising, taketh to himself the brightness of the stars,. So I assume the glory of women and men mine enemies.
7.13.2: All ye amang my rivals who behold me as I come to you, I seize the glory of my foes as the Sun, rising, theirs who sleep. A prayer to Savitar for prosperity
7.14.1: I praise this God, parent of heaven and earth, exceeding wiser possessed of real energy, giver of treasure, thinker dear to all,. Whose splendour is sublime, whose light shone brilliant in crea- tion, who, wise, and golden handed, in his beauty made the sky.
7.14.2: As thou, God! quickening, for our ancient father, sentest him height above and room about him, So unto us, O Savitar, send treasures, abundant, day by day, in shape of cattle.
7.14.3: Savitar, God, our household friend, most precious, hath sent our fathers life and power and riches. Let him drink Soma and rejoice when worshipped. Under his law even the Wanderer travels.
7.14.4: A charm to win divine favour and felicity I choose, O Savitar, that glorious favour, with fruitful energy and every blessing, Even this one’s teeming cow, erst milked by Kanva, thousand- streamed, milked for
7.15.1: happiness by the mighty. A prayer for prosperity Increase this man Brihaspati! Illume him, O Savitar, for high and happy fortune.
7.16.1: Sharpen him thoroughly though already sharpened: with glad acclaim let all the Gods receive him. A prayer for wealth and children
7.17.1: May the Ordainer give us wealth, Lord, ruler of the world of life: with full hand may he give to us. May Dhātar grant the worshipper henceforth imperishable life.
7.17.2: May we obtain the favour of the God who giveth every boon. To him may Dhātar grant all kinds of blessings who, craving children, serves him in his dwelling.
7.17.3: Him may the Gods invest with life eternal, yea, all the Gods and Aditi accordant. May this our gift please Savitar, Rāti, Dhātar, Prajāpati, and
7.17.4: 104 Agni Lord of Treasures. May Tvashtar, Vishnu, blessing him with children, give store ot riches to the sacrificer.
7.18.1: A prayer for rain Burst open, Prithvi, and cleave asunder this celestial cloud. Untie, O Dhātar—for thou canst—the bottle of the breast of heaven.
7.18.2: Let not the Sun’s heat burn, nor cold destroy her. Let Earth with all her quickening drops burst open. Even for her the waters flow, and fatness: where Soma is even there is bliss for ever.
7.19.1: A prayer for prosperity Prajapati engenders earthly creatures: may the benevolent Ordainer form them,
7.20.1: Having one common womb, and mind, and spirit. He who is. Lord of Plenty give me plenty! A prayer for prosperity and happiness
7.20.2: Anumati approve to-day our sacrifice among the Gods! May Agni bear mine offerings away for me the worshipper. Do thou, Anumati! approve, and grant us health and happiness.
7.20.3: Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, give us progeny. May he approving in return accord us wealth inexhaustible with store of children. Never may we be subject to his anger, but rest in his benevo- lence and mercy.
7.20.4: Thy name is easy to invoke, good leader! approved, Anumati and rich in bounty. Source of all bonds! fill up therewith our worship, and, Blest One! grant us wealth with goodly heroes.
7.20.5: Anumati hath come to this our worship well-formed to give good lands and valiant heroes: For her kind care hath blessed us. God-protected, may she assist the sacrifice we offer. Anumati became this All, whatever standeth or walketh, every- thing that moveth.
7.20.6: May we enjoy thy gracious love, O Goddess. Regard us, O Anu- mati, with favour. A funeral stanza With prayer come all together to the Lord of Heaven: he is the peerless one, far-reaching,
7.21.1: guest of men. He, God of ancient time, hath gained a recent thrall; to him alone is turned the path which all must tread.
7.22.1: To Savitar, or Yama invested with Savitar’s attributes Unto a thousand sages he hath given sight: thought, light is he in ranging all. The Bright One hath sent forth the Dawns, a closely gathered band,
7.22.2: Immaculate, unanimous, brightly refulgent in their homes. A charm to banish fiends and troubles 105
7.23.1: The fearful dream, and indigence, the monster, the malignant hags. All female fiends of evil name and wicked tongue we drive afar. A prayer for riches
7.24.1: What treasure hath been dug for us by Indra, by Agni, Visve- devas, tuneful Maruts, On us may Savitar whose laws are faithful, Prajāpati, and Heavenly Grace bestow it.
7.25.1: Praise of Vishnu and Varuna The early morning prayer hath come to Vishnu and Varuna, Lords through might, whom none hath equalled,
7.25.2: Gods by whose power the realms of air were stablished, strongest and most heroic in their vigour. The early prayer hath ever come to Vishnu and Varuna by that
7.26.1: God’s high power and statute. In whose control is all this world that shineth, all that hath powers to see and all that breatheth.
7.26.2: Praise of Vishnu I will declare the mighty deeds of Vishnu, of him who measured out the earthly regions, Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely
7.26.3: striding. Loud boast doth Vishnu make of this achievement, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming.
7.26.4: May he approach us from the farthest distance. Thou within whose three wide-extended paces all worlds and creatures have their habitation, Drink oil, thou homed in oil! promote the sacrificer more and more.
7.26.5: Through all this world strode Vishnu: thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep’s dust. Vishnu the guardian, he whom none deceiveth, made three steps, thenceforth.
7.26.6: Establishing these high decrees. Look ye on Vishnu’s works, whereby the friend of Indra, close- allied, Hath let his holy ways be seen.
7.26.7: The princes evermore behold that loftiest place where Vishnu is, Like an extended eye in heaven, From heaven, O Vishnu, or from earth, O Vishnu, or from the great far-spreading air’s mid region,
7.26.8: Fill both thy hands full of abundant treasures, and from the right and left bestow them freely. A prayer to Ida, Goddess of devotion May Idā with her statute dwell beside us, she in whose place the pious purge and cleanse
7.27.1: them. She, mighty, Soma-decked, whose foot drops fatness, meet for All-Gods, hath come to aid our worship.
7.28.1: 106 Praise of the sacrificial utensils Blest be the Broom, may the Mace bring a blessing, and may the
7.29.1: Altar and the Hatchet bless us. Worshipful Gods, may they accept this worship, lovers of sacri- fice, and sacrificers. To Agni and Vishnu
7.29.2: This is your glorious might, Agni and Vishnu! Ye drink the essence of the mystic butter. Placing in every home seven costly treasures. Let your tongue stretch to take the offered fatness.
7.30.1: Ye love the great law, Agni Vishnu! joying, ye feast on mystic essences of butter, Exalted in each house with fair laudation. Let your tongue stretch to take the offered fatness. A charm to be used when the eyes are anointed
7.31.1: Heaven, Earth, and Mitra here have caused mine eyes to be- anointed well, Savitar, Brāhmanaspati take care that they be duly balmed! A prayer for the overthrow of enemies
7.32.1: Rouse us to-day O Indra, Maghavan, hero, with thy best pos- sible and varied succours, May he who hateth us fall low beneath us, and him whom we detest let life abandon. A prayer to Agni for long life
7.33.1: We bringing homage have approached the friend who seeks our wondering praise, Young, strengthener of the sacrifice. May he bestow long life on me. A prayer for long life, children, and riches
7.34.1: Let Pūshan, let the Maruts, let Brihaspati pour forth on me; This present Agni pour on me children and riches in a stream! May he bestow long life on me.
7.35.1: A prayer for freedom from sin and the overthrow of enemies Agni, drive off my rivals born and living, repel those yet unborn, O Jātavedas.
7.35.2: Cast down beneath my feet mine adversaries. In Aditi’s regard may we be sinless. A prayer for the prosperity of a King and his kingdom Subdue with conquering might his other rivals, those yet unborn repel, O Jātavedas.
7.35.3: For great felicity protect this kingdom, and in this man let all the Gods be joyful. Hae quot tibi sunt venae atque arteriae harum omnium os tibi lapide occlusi. 107
7.36.1: Uteri tui summam partem inferam facio: ne tibi soboles neque filius eveniat. Sterilem et infecundam te facio: lapidem tuum, operimentum facio. A charm to be pronounced by bride and bridegroom
7.37.1: Sweet are the glances of our eyes, our faces are as smooth as balm, Within thy bosom harbour me; one spirit dwell in both of us! A nuptial charm to be spoken by the bride
7.38.1: With this my robe, inherited from Manu, I envelop thee, So that thou mayst be all mine own and give no thought to other dames. A maiden’s love-charm
7.38.2: I dig this Healing Herb that makes my lover look on me and weep; That bids the parting friend return and kindly greets him as he comes. This Herb wherewith the Asuri drew Indra downward from the
7.38.3: Gods, With this same Herb I draw thee close that I may be most dear to thee. Thou art the peer of Soma, yea, thou art the equal of the Sun, p. a285
7.38.4: The peer of all the Gods art thou: therefore we call thee hither— ward. I am the speaker here, not thou: speak thou where the assembly meets. Thou shalt be mine and only mine, and never mention other dames.
7.38.5: If thou art far away beyond the rivers, far away from men, This Herb shall seem to bind thee fast and bring thee back my prisoner. A sacrificial charm for rain and prosperity
7.39.1: May he establish in our home the master of riches, gladdening with rain in season, Mighty, strong-winged, celestial, dropping moisture, Bull of the plants and embryo of waters. A prayer for prosperity
7.40.1: We call Sarasvān, under whose protection all cattle wander, to preserve and aid us, Him in whose ordinance abide the waters, to whose command the Lord of Plenty listens. Abiding here let us invoke Sarasvān, the seat of riches, glorious, wealth-increaser,
7.40.2: Him who inclines and gives to him who worships, the rich pos- sessor and the Lord of Fulness. A prayer for prosperity
7.41.1: Observing men, and viewing home, the Falcon hath cleft his swift way over wastes and waters. May he, with Indra for a friend, auspicious, traversing all air’s lower realms, come hither.
7.41.2: The heavenly Falcon, viewing men, well-pinioned, strength-giver, hundred-footed, hundred nested, Shall give us treasure which was taken from us. May it be rich in food among our Fathers. 108
7.42.1: A prayer for delivery from sin and sickness Scatter and drive away, Soma and Rudra, the sickness that hath come within our dwelling, Afar into the distance chase Destruction, and even from commit- ted sin release us.
7.42.2: Lay on our bodies, O ye twain, O Soma and Rudra, all those balms that heal diseases. Set free and draw away the sin committed, which we have still inherent in our persons. A charm against lightning
7.43.1: Some of thy words bode weal and some misfortune: thou scat- terest them all with friendly feeling. Deep within this three words are laid: among them one hath flown off even as the sound was
7.44.1: uttered. In praise of Indra and Vishnu Ye twain have conquered, and have not been vanquished: not either of the pair hath been
7.45.1: defeated. Ye, Indra Vishnu, when ye fought your battle; produced this infinite with three divisions. A charm against jealousy
7.45.2: Brought hitherward from Sindhu, from a folk of every mingled race, Fetched from afar, thou art I deem, a balm that cureth. jealousy. As one with water quencheth fire, so calm this lover’s jealousy,
7.46.1: Like heat of fire that burneth here, or flame that rageth through the wood. A charm for offspring and prosperity O broad-tressed Sinivāli, thou who art the sister of the Gods,
7.46.2: Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny. Present the sacrifice to her, to Sinivāli, Queen of men, Beauti- ful-fingered, lovely-armed, prolific, bearing many a child.
7.46.3: Thou who as Queen of men art Indra’s equal, a Goddess coming with a thousand tresses, To thee our sacrifices are performed, O Consort of Vishnu Goddess, urge thy Lord to bounty!
7.47.1: A prayer for wealth and birth of a son Oft in this sacrifice with favoured cry I call Kuhū, beneficent Goddess, skilled in all her works.
7.47.2: May she vouchsafe us wealth with every boon, and give a, hero meet for praise who gives a hundred gifts. Kuhl), the Queen of Gods and immortality, called to assist, enjoy this sacrifice of’ ours!
7.48.1: Let her, desirous of our worship, hear to-day: may she, intelligent, give increase of our wealth. A prayer for prosperity and the birth of a son
7.48.2: I call on Rākā with hair laud and reverent cry: may she, auspicious, hear us and herself observe. With never-breaking needle may she sew her work, and send a glorious man who gives a
7.49.1: hundred gifts. All thy kind favours, Rākā! lovely in their form, wherewith thou grantest treasures to the man who gives,
7.49.2: With these come thou to us this day benevolent, O blessed one, bestowing wealth of thousand sorts. A prayer for children and booty
7.50.1: May the Gods’ Consorts aid us of their own free will, help us to offspring and the winning of the spoil. May Goddesses who quickly listen shelter us, both those on earth and they within the waters’
7.50.2: realm. May the Dames, wives of Gods, enjoy our presents, Rāt, Asvini Indrāni and Agnāyi;
7.50.3: May Rodasi and Varunāni hear us, and Goddesses come at the matrons’ season. A gambler’s prayer for success in gaming As evermore the lightning flash strikes, irresistible, the tree,
7.50.4: So, irresistible, may I conquer the gamblers with the dice. From every side, from hale and sick, impotent to defend them- selves, May all the fortune of the folk as winnings pass into my hands.
7.50.5: I pray to Agni, him who guards his treasure: here, won by homage, may he pile our winnings. As ‘twere with racing cars I bring my presents: duly with reverence, let me laud the Maruts. With thee to aid us may we win the treasure: do thou assist our side in every battle.
7.50.6: Give us wide room and easy way, O Indra; break down, O Maghavan, the foemen’s valour. I have completely cleaned thee out, won from thee what thou keptest back.
7.50.7: As a wolf tears and rends a sheep, so do I tear thy stake away. Yea, by superior play one gains advantage: in time he piles his spoil as doth a gambler. He overwhelms with wealth’s inherent powers the devotee who keeps not back his riches.
7.50.8: May we all, much-invoked! repel with cattle want that brings sin, hunger with store of barley. May we uninjured, first among the princes, obtain possessions by our own exertions. My right hand holds my winnings fast, and in my left is victory.
7.50.9: I would that I were winner of cattle and horses, wealth and gold. Dice, give me play that bringeth fruit as ‘twere a cow with flowing milk! And, as the bowstring binds, the bow, unite me with a stream of gains.
7.51.1: A prayer for Brihaspati’s and Indra’s protection Brihaspati protect us from the sinner, from rearward, from above, and from below us! May Indra from the front and from the centre, as friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and
7.52.1: freedom. A prayer for peace and concord Give us agreement with our own, with strangers give us unity:
7.52.2: Do ye, O Asvins, in this place join us in sympathy and love. May we agree in mind, agree in purpose: let us not fight against the heavenly spirit. Around us rise no din of frequent slaughter, nor Indra’s arrow fly, for day is present!
7.53.1: A charm to recover a sick man at the point of death As thou, Brihaspati, from the curse hast saved us, from dwel- ling yonder in the realm of Yama,
7.53.2: The Asvins, leeches of the Gods, O Agni, have chased Death far from us with mighty powers. Move both together; do not leave the body. Let both the breathings stay for thee united. Waxing in strength live thou a hundred autumns. Thy noblest guardian and thy lord is Agni.
7.53.3: Return, thy life now vanished into distance! Return, the breath thou drawest and exhalest! Agni hath snatched it from Destruction’s bosom: into thyself again I introduce it. Let not the vital breath he draws forsake him, let not his expiration part and leave him.
7.53.4: I give him over to the Seven Rishis: let them conduct him to old age in safety. Enter him, both ye breaths, like two draught-oxen entering their stall. Let him, the treasure of old age, still wax in strength, uninjured,. here.
7.53.5: I send thee back thy vital breath; I drive Consumption far from thee, May Agni here, most excellent, sustain our life on every side. From out the depth of darkness, we, ascending to the highest heaven,
7.53.6: Have come to the sublimest light, to Sūrya, God among the. Gods. A charm to obtain knowledge of the Veda
7.53.7: We worship holy Verse and Song, by which they carry out their acts, Shining in order’s seat these twain present the sacrifice to Gods. As I have asked about Verse, Song, Sacrifice, strength, force,.
7.54.1: Yajus-text, So never let this lore that I have sought forsake me, Lord of Might!
7.54.2: A charm to ensure a prosperous journey Thy downward paths from heaven, whereby thou hast raised all the world to life, Give us in gracious love, good Lord!
7.55.1: A charm against poisonous bites and stings Whether it came from viper, from black snake or snake with transverse stripes, Or Kankaparvan’s bite, this herb hath made the poison power- less.
7.56.1: Honey-born, honey-dropping, rich in honey, honeysweet, this herb, Is medicine that heals the wound and kills the gnat that bites and stings. Whatever bit, or sucked thy blood, we summon thence away from thee
7.56.2: The ineffectual poison of the little sharply-stinging gnat. Thou here who crookest wicked jaws, thou tortuous, jointless, limbless thing, 111
7.56.3: These jaws thou, Brāhmanaspati! shalt bend together like a reed. This scorpion here that creeps along, low on the ground and powerless— I have removed his poison and then utterly demolished him.
7.56.4: No strength in thy two arms hast thou, nor in thy head, nor in thy waist: Then what is that small thing thou so viciously bearest in thy tail? The emmets make a meal of thee and peahens tear and mangle thee:
7.56.5: All ye are crying out, In sooth the scorpion’s poison hath no strength. Thou creature who inflictest wounds both with thy mouth and with thy tail, No poison in thy mouth hast thou: what at thy tail’s root will there be?
7.56.6: A charm for some physical disorder Whatever trouble hath disturbed and shaken me—I speak with hope, I move, imploring, ‘mid the folk
7.56.7: What harm my body in myself hath suffered, now let Sarasvati relieve with fatness. Seven flow for him, the youth on whom the Maruts wait: the sons have taught the Father everlasting laws.
7.56.8: Both worlds are his: both shine belonging unto him. Both move together: both, as his possession thrive. An invitation to Indra and Varuna
7.57.1: True to laws, Indra Varuna, drinkers of the juice, quaff this pressed Soma which shall give you rapturous joy! Let sacrifice, your car, to entertain the Gods, approach its rest- ing-place that they may drink
7.57.2: thereof. O Indra Varuna, drink your fill, ye heroes, of this effectual and sweetest Soma. This juice was shed by us that ye might quaff it. On this trimmed grass be seated and rejoice
7.58.1: you. An imprecation Like a tree struck by lightning may the man be withered from the root.
7.58.2: Who curseth us who curse not him, or, when we curse him. curseth us. A parting traveller’s address to the houses of his village I, prudent, bringing power, a treasure-winner, with amicable eye that strikes no terror,
7.59.1: Come, praising and kind-thoughted, to these houses: be not afraid of me, be glad and joyful. Let these delightful Houses that are rich in power and store of milk, Replete with wealth and standing firm, become aware of our approach.
7.60.1: These Houses we invoke, whereon the distant exile sets his thought, Wherein dwells many a friendly heart: let them beware of our approach. Thus greeted, ye of ample wealth, friends who enjoy delightful sweets.
7.60.2: Be ever free from hunger, free from thirst! Ye Houses, fear us not. Kind greeting to the cattle here, kind greeting to the goats and sheep! Then, of the food within our homes, kind greeting to the plea- sant drink!
7.60.3: Full of refreshment, full of charms, of laughter and felicity, Be ever free from hunger, free from thirst! Ye Houses, fear us not. 112
7.60.4: Stay here, and come not after me: prosper in every form and shape. With happy fortune will I come! Grow more abundant still through me! A prayer for sacred knowledge and its fruits
7.60.5: Since, Agni, with our fervent zeal we undergo austerity, May we be dear to Sacred Lore, may we be wise and live long lives. Agni, we practise acts austere, we undergo austerity.
7.60.6: So listening to Holy Lore may we grow wise and full of days. A prayer for the overthrow of enemies Like a car-warrior, Agni here, grown mighty, Lord of the brave,
7.60.7: Chief Priest, hath conquered footmen. Laid on earth’s centre he hath flashed and glittered. Low may he lay our enemies beneath us. A prayer for deliverance from affliction
7.61.1: We call with lauds from his most lofty dwelling victorious Agni, conqueror in battles. May he conveyus over all distresses, may the God Agni bear us past our troubles. A charm to avert an evil omen
7.61.2: From all that woe and trouble may the Waters save and rescue me, Whate’er the Raven, black of hue, flying out hither ward, hath dropped. May Agni Gārhapatya save and set me free from all this guilt.
7.62.1: Which the black Raven with thy mouth, O Nirriti, hath wiped away. A charm against imprecation and threatened evils With retroverted fruit hast thou, O Apāmārga, sprung and grown.
7.63.1: Hence into distance most remote drive every curse away from, me. Whatever evil we have done, whatever vile or sinful act, With thee, O Apāmārga, who lookest all ways, we wipe it off.
7.64.1: If with the cripple we have lived, whose teeth are black and nails deformed, With thee, O Apāmārga, we wipe all that ill away from us. A prayer to Vāk
7.64.2: If it was in the wind or air’s mid-region, if it was in the trees or in the bushes, To meet whose utterance forth streamed the cattle, may that. Celestial Power again approach us.
7.65.1: A priest’s prayer to the Agnayo Dhishnyāh May sense return to me again, and spirit, return my Sacred Power and my possessions!
7.65.2: Again let fires, aflame on lesser altars, each duly stationed, here succeed and prosper. 113 A prayer for children and prosperity
7.65.3: Sarasvati, in thy decrees, Goddess, in thy celestial laws, Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny. Here is, Sarasvati, thy fat libation, this sacrifice passing to the mouth of Fathers.
7.66.1: These most auspicious offerings have ascended to thee: through, these may we be full of sweetness. Be kind and most auspicious, be gracious to us, Sarasvati, May we be ever in thy sight.
7.67.1: A prayer for prosperity May the wind kindly breathe on us, may the Sun warm us. pleasantly. May days pass happily for us, may night draw near delightfully, may dawn break joyfully for
7.68.1: May, in accord with Death, Destruction ruin his offering before it gain fulfilment. For him may sorcerers, Destruction, demons strike and prevent fulfilment through their falsehood.
7.68.2: Let Gods, by Indra sent, destroy his butter, and let his sacrifice be ineffective. Let the two Sovrans, swift to come, like falcons swooping on their prey, Destroy the butter of the foe whoever plots to injure us.
7.69.1: I seize thine arms and draw them back, I bind a bandage on thy mouth. I with the anger of the God Agni have killed thy sacrifice. Behind thy back I tie thine arms, I bind a bandage on thy mouth:
7.70.1: With the terrific Agni’s wrath have I destroyed thy sacrifice. In praise of Agni We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni! thee a sage,
7.70.2: Bold in thy colour day by day, destroyer of the treacherous foe. An invitation to Indra Rise up and look upon the share of Indra fixt by ritual use.
7.70.3: Whether ye poured libation dressed or took delight in it un- cooked. Libation is prepared. Come to us, Indra: the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their treasures sit around thee, waiting like heads of houses for their wandering
7.70.4: chieftain. Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well dressed, I fancy, is this new oblation. Quaff thickened milk of noon’s libation, Indra, well pleased, O
7.70.5: Thunderer, famed for many an exploit! An invitation to the Asvins 114
7.71.1: Inflamed is Agni, Heroes! charioteer of heaven. The caldron boils: the meath is drained to be your food. For we, O Asvins, singers sprung from many a house, invite you to be present at our
7.72.1: Pure with the Gods is sacrifice with cry of Hail! That is the Asvins’ cup whence Gods are wont to drink. Yea, the Immortal Ones accept it, one and all, and come to kiss that cup with the Gandharva’s
7.72.2: mouth. Milk, molten butter offered when the mornings break,—this is your portion, Asvins! Come ye hitherward.
7.73.1: Lords of the brave, balm-lovers, guards of sacrifice, drink ye the warm libation in the light of heaven. Let the warm drink approach you with its Hotar-priest: let the
7.73.10: Adhvaryu come to you with store of milk. Come, O ye Asvins, taste the meath that hath been drained, drink of the milk provided by this radiant cow.
7.73.11: Come hither, quickly come, thou milker of the kine; into the caldron pour milk of the radiant cow. Most precious Savitar hath looked upon the heaven. After
7.73.2: Dawn’s going-forth he sends his light abroad. I invocate this milch-cow good for milking, so that the milker, deft of hand, may milk her. May Savitar give goodliest stimulation. The caldron hath been warmed. Let him proclaim it.
7.73.3: She, sovran of all treasures, is come hither yearning in spirit for her calf, and lowing. May this cow yield her milk for both the Asvins, and may she prosper to our great advantage. As dear house-friend, guest welcome in the dwelling, to this our sacrifice come thou who
7.73.4: knowest. And, Agni, having scattered all assailants, bring to us the posses- sions of our foemen. Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni! Most excellent be thine effulgent splendours!
7.73.5: Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us. Fortunate mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy. Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and, coming hither, drink the limpid water.
7.73.6: A charm to cure pustules, sores, or scrofulous swellings (apachitas) Black is the mother, we have heard, from whom the red-hued Pustules sprang.
7.73.7: With the divine ascetic’s root I pierce and penetrate them all. I pierce the foremost one of these, I perforate the middlemost, And here I cut the hindermost asunder like a lock of hair.
7.73.8: With spell that Tvashtar sent to us I have dispelled thy jealousy. We mitigate and pacify the anger that thou feltest, Lord! Lord of religious rites, by law, anointed, shine thou forth here for ever friendly-minded.
7.73.9: So may we all with children, Jātavedas! worship and humbly wait on thee enkindled. A blessing on cows 115
7.74.1: Let not a thief or wicked man possess you: let not the dart of Rudra come anear you, Prolific, shining in the goodly pasture, drinking at pleasant pools the limpid water.
7.74.2: Ye know the place and rest content, close-gathered, called by many a name. Come to me, Goddesses, with Gods Bedew with streams of fatness us, this cattle-pen, and all this place.
7.74.3: A charm to cure scrofulous pustules and scrofula Rapidly dropping, quick to drop, more evil than the evil ones, More sapless than a dried-up bone, swifter than salt to melt away.
7.74.4: Pustules that rise upon the neck, Pustules upon the shoulder- joints, Pustules that, falling of themselves, spring up on every twofold limb: I have expelled and banished all Scrofula harboured in the head,
7.75.1: And that which bores the breast-bone through, and that which settles in the sole. Scrofula flies borne on by wings: it penerates and holds the man. Here is the cure of either kind, the chronic and the transient.
7.75.2: We know thine origin, Scrofula! know whence thou, Scrofula, art born. How hast thou then struck this man here, him in whose house we sacrifice? Boldly drink Soma from the beaker, Indra! hero in war for treasure! Vritra-slayer.
7.76.1: Fill thyself full at the mid-day libation: thyself possessing riches grant us riches. An incantation against an enemy Ye Maruts, full of fiery heat, accept this offering brought for you
7.76.2: To help us, ye who slay the foe. Maruts, the man who filled with rage against us beyond our thoughts would harm us, O ye Vasus,
7.76.3: May he be tangled in the toils of Mischief: smite ye him down with your most flaming weapon. Each year come, friends to man, the tuneful Maruts, dwelling in spacious mansions, trooped
7.76.4: together. Exhilarating, gladdening full of fiery heat, may they deliver us from binding bonds of sin. A charm for a prince’s prosperity
7.76.5: I free thee from the cord, I loose the bond, I loose the fastening. Even here, perpetual, Agni, wax thou strong. I with celestial prayer appoint thee, Agni, maintainer of this man in princely powers.
7.76.6: Here brightly shine for us with wealth: declare thou to Gods this favoured giver of oblations. A hymn to the New Moon Night of the New-born Moon, whatever fortune the Gods who dwell with greatness have
7.77.1: assigned thee, Therewith fulfil our sacrifice, all-baunteous! Blessed One, grant us wealth with manly offspring.
7.77.2: I am the New Moon’s Night, the good and pious are my in- habitants, these dwell within me. In me have Gods of both the spheres, and Sādhyas, with Indra as their chief, all met together. 116
7.77.3: The Night hath come, the gatherer of treasures, bestowing strength, prosperity, and riches. To New Moon’s Night let us present oblation: pouring out strength, with milk hath she come hither.
7.78.1: Night of New Moon! ne’er hath been born another than thou embracing all these forms and natures, May we have what we longed for when we brought thee obla- tions: may we be the lords of
7.78.2: riches. A hymn to the Full Moon Full in the front, full rearward, from the middle the Full Moon’s
7.79.1: Night hath conquered in the battle. In her: may we, dwelling with Gods and greatness, feast in the height of heaven, on strengthening viands.
7.79.2: To him, the Full Moon’s mighty Bull, we pay our solemn sacri- fice. May he bestow upon us wealth unwasting, inexhaustible. No one but thou, Prajāpati, none beside thee, pervading, gave to all these forms their being.
7.79.3: Grant us our hearts’ desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession. First was the Full Moon meet for adoration among the days and in the nights’ deep darkness. Into thy heaven, O Holy One, have entered those pious men who honour thee with worship.
7.79.4: A hymn to the New Moon Forward and backward by their wondrous power move these two youths, disporting, round the ocean.
7.80.1: One views all living things, and thou, the other, art born again arranging times and seasons. Thou art re-born for ever new: thou marchest, ensign of days, in forefront of the mornings. Marching thou dealest to the Gods their portion. Thou lengthe- nest, Moon! the days of man’s
7.80.2: existence. O spray of Soma, Lord of Wars! all-perfect verily art thou. Make me all-perfect, Beauteous One! in riches and in progeny.
7.80.3: Thou art the New Moon, fair to see, thou art complete in every part. May I be perfect, fully blest in every way in steeds and kine, in children, cattle, home, and wealth.
7.80.4: Inflate thee with his vital breath who hathes us and whom we detest. May we grow rich in steeds and kine, in children, cattle, houses, wealth. With that unwasting stalk which Gods, unwasting Gods, in- crease and eat,
7.81.1: May Varuna, Brihaspati, and Indra, the Lords and Guardians of the world, increase us. In praise of Agni Sing with fair laud the combat for the cattle. Bestow upon us excellent possessions.
7.81.2: Lead to the Gods the sacrifice we offer: let streams of oil flow pure and full of sweetness. Agni I first appropriate with power, with splendour, and with might. I give myself children and lengthened life, with Hail! take Agni to myself.
7.81.3: Even here do thou, O Agni, stablish wealth: let not oppressors injure thee by thinking of thee first. Light be thy task of ruling, Agni, with, thy power: may he who worships thee wax strong,
7.81.4: invincible. 117 Agni hath looked upon the spring of Morning, looked on the days, the earliest Jātavedas.

7.111.1: Release me from the curse’s bond and plague that comes from Varuna; 122

7.118.1: King Soma clothe thee! Varuna give thee what is more than ample, and in thy triumph let the Gods be joyful. 123

8.1.1: A charm to recover a dying man Homage to Death the Ender! May thy breathings, inward and outward, still remain within
8.1.10: thee. Here stay this man united with his spirit in the Sun’s realm, the world of life eternal!
8.1.11: Bhaga hath lifted up this man, and Soma with his filaments, Indra and Agni, and the Gods the Maruts, raised him up to health.
8.1.12: Here is thy spirit, here thy breath, here is thy life, here is thy soul: By a celestial utterance we raise thee from Destruction’s bonds.
8.1.13: Up from this place, O man, rise! sink not downward, casting away the bonds of Death that hold thee.
8.1.14: Be not thou parted from this world, from sight of Agni and the Sun.
8.1.15: Purely for thee breathe Wind and Mātarisvan, and let the Waters rain on thee their nectar.
8.1.16: The Sun shall shine with healing on thy body; Death shall have mercy on thee: do not leave us!
8.1.17: Upward must be thy way, O man, not downward: with life and mental vigour I endow thee. Ascend this car eternal, lightly rolling; then full of years shalt thou address the meeting.
8.1.18: Let not thy soul go thither, nor be lost to us: slight not the living, go not where the Fathers are.
8.1.19: Let all the Gods retain thee here in safety. Yearn not for the departed ones, for those who lead men far away.
8.1.2: Rise up from darkness into light: come, both thy hands we clasp in ours. Let not the black dog and the brindled seize thee, two warders of the way sent forth by Yama.
8.1.20: Come hither; do not hesitate: with mind averted stay not there. Forbear to tread this path, for it is awful: that path I speak of which thou hast not travelled.
8.1.21: Enter it not, O man; this way is darkness: forward is danger, hitherward is safety. Thy guardians be the Fires within the Waters, thy guardian be the Fire which men enkindle.
8.1.3: Thy guardian be Vaisvānara Jātavedas; let not celestial Fire with lightning burn thee. Let not the Flesh-Consumer plot against thee: depart thou far away from the Destroyer.
8.1.4: Be Heaven and Earth and Sun and Moon thy keepers, and from the dart of Gods may Air protect thee.
8.1.5: May Vigilance and Watchfulness protect thee, Sleepless and Slumberless keep guard above thee!
8.1.6: Let Guardian and let Wakeful be thy warders. Let these be thy preservers, these thy keepers. All hail to these, to these be lowly worship!
8.1.7: May saving Savitar, Vāyu, Indra, Dhātar restore thee to com- munion with the living. Let not thy vigour or thy breath forsake thee: we recall thy life.
8.1.8: Let not the fiend with snapping jaws, nor darkness find thee: tongue, holy grass: how shouldst thou perish?
8.1.9: May the Ādityas and the Vasus, Indra and Agni raise thee and to health restore thee. The Sky hath raised thee, and the Earth, Prajāpati hath raised thee up.
8.2.1: The Plants and Herbs with Soma as their King have rescued thee from Death. Here let this man, O Gods, remain: let him not go to yonder world.
8.2.10: 124 We rescue him from Mrityu with a charm that hath a thousand powers.
8.2.11: I have delivered thee from Death. Strength-givers smelt and fashion thee! Let not she-fiends with wild loose locks, or fearful howlers yell at thee.
8.2.12: I have attained and captured thee: thou hast returned restored to youth. Perfect in body: so have I found all thy sight and all thy life.
8.2.13: Life hath breathed on thee; light hath come: darkness hath past away from thee. Far from thee we have buried Death, buried Destruction and:
8.2.15: Seize to thyself this trust of life for ever: thine be longevity which nothing shortens. Thy spirit and thy life again I bring thee: die not, nor vanish into mist and darkness.
8.2.16: Come to the light of living men, come hither: I draw thee to a life of hundred autumns. Loosing the bonds of Death, the curse that holds thee, I give thee age of very long duration.
8.2.17: Thy breath have I recovered from the Wind, thy vision from the Sun.
8.2.18: Thy mind I stablish and secure within thee: feel in thy members,. use thy tongue, conversing. I blow upon thee with the breath of bipeds and quadrupeds, as on a fire new-kindled.
8.2.19: To thee, O Death, and to thy sight and breath have I paid reverence. Let this man live, let him not die: we raise him, we recover him.
8.2.2: I make for him a healing balm. O Death, forbear to slay this man. Here for sound health I invocate a living animating plant,
8.2.20: Preserving, queller of disease, victorious, full of power and might. Seize him not, but encourage and release him: here let him stay, though thine, in all his
8.2.21: vigour. Bhava and Sarva, pity and protect him: give him full life and drive away misfortunes.
8.2.22: Comfort him, Death, and pity him: let him arise and pass away, Unharmed, with all his members, hearing well, with old, may he through hundred years win

8.2.24: preserved thee. Far have I banished flesh-consuming Agni: I place a rampart for thy life’s protection.
8.2.25: Saving him from that misty path of thine which cannot be defined. From that descent of thine, O Death, we make for him a shield of prayer.

8.2.27: I chase away. Far off we drive Malignity, Destruction, Pisāchas banqueters on flesh, and Grāhi.
8.2.28: And all the demon kind, the brood of sin, like darkness, we dispel. I win thy life from Agni, from the living everlasting Jātavedas.
8.2.3: This I procure for thee, that thou, undying, mayst not suffer harm, that thou mayst be content, that all be well with thee.

8.4.2: Rākshasas, O Agni, with thy sharpened glow, with rays that flash with points of flame.

8.5.12: Lords of men, animate these my prayers. In your impetuous manner think ye both thereon: destroy those evil spirits, kill the
8.5.13: treacherous fiends. Indra and Soma, let the wicked have no bliss whoso at any time- attacks and injures us.
8.5.14: Whoso accuses me with words of falsehood when I pursue my way with guileless spirit, May he, the speaker of untruth, be, Indra! like water which the hollowed hand compresses.
8.5.15: Those who destroy, as is their wont, the simple, and with their evil natures harm the righteous,
8.5.16: May Soma give them over to the serpent, or to the lap of Nirriti consign them.
8.5.17: O Agni, whosoever seeks to injure the essence of our food, kine, steeds, or bodies, May he, the adversary, thief, and robber, sink to destruction,. both himself and offspring.
8.5.18: May he be swept away, himself and children; may all the three earths press him down beneath them.
8.5.19: May his fair glory, O ye Gods, be blighted, who in the day or night would fain destroy us. The prudent finds it easy to distinguish the true and false: their words oppose each other.
8.5.2: Of these two that which is the true and honest Soma protects, and brings the false to nothing. Never doth Soma aid and guide the wicked or him who falsely claims the Warrior’s title.
8.5.20: He slays the fiend and him who speaks untruly: both lie entan- gled in the noose of Indra. As if I worshipped deities of falsehood, or thought vain thoughts about the Gods, O Agni!
8.5.21: Why art thou angry with us, Jātavedas? Destruction fall on those who lie against thee! So may I die this day if I have harassed any man’s life, or if I be a demon.
8.5.22: Yea, may he lose all his ten sons together who with false tongue hath called me Yātudhāna. May Indra slay him with a mighty weapon, and let the vilest of all creatures perish,
8.5.3: The fiend who says that he is pure, who calls me a demon though devoid of demon nature. She too who wanders like an owl at night-time, hiding her body in her guile and malice,
8.5.4: May she fall downward into endless caverns. May press-stones with loud ring destroy the demons.
8.5.5: Spread out, ye Maruts, search among the people: seize ye and grind the Rākshasas to pieces, Who fly abroad, transformed to birds, at night-time, and sully and pollute our holy worship.
8.5.6: Hurl down from heaven thy bolt of stone, O Indra: sharpen it, Maghavan, made keen by Soma.
8.5.7: Forward, behind, and from above and under, smite down the demons with thy rocky weapon. They fly, the demon dogs, and, bent on mischief, fain would they harm indomitable Indra.
8.5.8: 128 Sakra makes sharp his weapon for the wicked: now let him cast his bolt at fiendish wizards.
8.5.9: Indra hath ever been the fiends’ destroyer who spoil oblations of the Gods’ invokers. Yea, Sakra, like an axe that splits the timber, assails and sma- shes them like earthen vessels.
8.6.1: Destroy the fiend shaped like an owl or owlet, destroy him in. the form of dog or cuckoo. Destroy him shaped as eagle or as vulture: as with a stone, O
8.6.10: Indra, crush the demon. Let not the fiend of witchcraft-workers reach us: may Dawn. drive off the couples of
8.6.11: Kimidins. Earth keep us safe from earthly woe and trouble! From grief that comes from heaven Mid-air
8.6.12: preserve us! Indra destroy the demon, male and female, joying and triumph- ing in arts of magic!
8.6.13: Let the fools’ gods with bent necks fall and perish, and see no. more the Sun when he arises. Look, each one, hither, look around. Indra and Soma, watch ye well.
8.6.14: Cast forth your weapon at the fiends: against the sorcerers hurl your bolt. A charm accompanying investiture with an amulet Upon the strong is bound the strong, this magic cord, this Amu- let,
8.6.15: Potent, foe-slayer, served by valiant heroes, happy and fortu- nate defence. This Charm, foe-slayer, served by many heroes, strong, power- ful, victorious, and mighty,
8.6.16: goes bravely forth to meet and ruin witchcraft. With this same Amulet wise Indra routed the Asuras, with this he slaughtered Vritra, With this he won this pair, both Earth and Heaven, and made the sky’s four regions his
8.6.17: possession. May this encircling magic cord, this Amulet of Srāktya wood,
8.6.18: Mighty, subduing enemies, keep us secure on every side. This Agni hath declared, Soma declared it, Brihaspati, and Savitar, and Indra.
8.6.19: So may these Gods whom I have set before me oppose with saving charms and banish witchcraft.
8.6.2: I have obscured the heaven and earth, yea, and the daylight and the sun. So may these Gods whom I have set before me oppose with saving charms and banish witchcraft.
8.6.20: Whoever for his armour takes an amulet of the Srāktya tree, Like the Sun risen up to heaven, quells witchcraft with superior might.
8.6.21: With Amulet of Srāktya wood, as with a thoughtful Rishi’s aid, In every fight have I prevailed; I smite the foes and Rākshasas. All witchcraft of Angirases,”all witchcraft wrought by Asuras,
8.6.22: All witchcraft self-originate, and all that others have prepared, May these depart to both remotest spaces, past ninety ample water-floods.
8.6.23: May the Gods bind the Charm on him for armour, Indra, and Vishnu, Savitar Rudra, Agni, Prajāpati, sublimest Parameshlhin, Virāj, Vaisvānara, and all the Rishis.
8.6.24: Thou art the chief of all the plants, even as a bull among the beasts. A tiger of the beasts of prey. Him whom we sought for have we found, him lying near in wait
8.6.25: for us. A tiger verily is he, he is a lion, and a bull, Subduer of his foes is he, the man who wears this Amulet.
8.6.26: No mortal beings slay him, no Gāndharvas, no Apsarases; O’er all the regions he is king, the man who wears this Amulet.
8.6.3: 129 Kasyapa formed and fashioned thee, Kasyapa raised and sent thee forth. Indra wore thee, and, wearing thee, won in the wrestling-match with man.

8.6.5: Meet him and smite him, Indra! with thy hundred-knotted thunderbolt. Verily let this Amulet, circular, potent, conquering, Happy and fortunate defence, preserve thy children and thy wealth.
8.6.6: Brave Indra, set before us light, peace and security from below, Peace and security from above, peace and security from behind.
8.6.7: My coat of mail is Heaven and Earth, my coat of mail is Day and Sun: A coat of mail may Indra and Agni and Dhātar grant to me. Not all the Gods may pierce, all leagued together, the vast strong shield which Indra gives,
8.6.8: and Agni. May that great shield on all sides guard my body, that to full old my life may be extended.
8.6.9: Let the Gods’ Charm be bound on me to keep me safe from every ill. Come ye and enter all within this pillar, the safe-guard of the body, thrice-defended. In this let Indra lay a store of valour: approach ye Gods, and enter it together,
8.7.1: For his long life, to last a hundred autumns, that to full age his days may be extended. Lord of the clan who brings, us bliss, fiend-slayer, queller of the foe,

8.7.25: Kumbhamushkas, these, Drive thou, O Brāhmanaspati, far from this girl with vigilance. Sightless and with distorted eyes, impotent. woman less be they.

8.7.27: The Bristly-haired, the Maniac-haired, the Biter, and the Groper-fiend, The Creeper-near, the Copper-hued, the Snouty, and the Saluda,
8.7.28: With foot and heel kick over, as a hasty cow her milking-pan. If one should touch thy coming babe or kill thine infant newly born,
8.7.3: The yellow Plant with mighty bow shall pierce him even to the heart. Those who kill infants unawares, and near the new-made mothers lie, Let Pinga chase the amorous Gandharvas as wind chases cloud.
8.7.4: Let it maintain the genial seed: let the laid embryo rest secure. Let both strong Healers, to be worn within the girdle, guard the babe.
8.7.5: From the Kimīdin, for thy lord and children, Pinga shield thee well, From Sāyaka, and Nagnaka, Tangalva, and Pavīnasa. From the five-footed, fingerless, from the four-eyed, the double- faced,

8.7.7: Feeders on babes unborn, long-haired, far from this place we banish these. Shy slinkers from the Sun, as slinks a woman from her husband’s sire, Deep down into the heart of these let Baja and let Pinga pierce.
8.7.8: Pinga, preserve the babe at birth, make not the boy a female child. Let not Egg-eaters mar the germs: drive the Kimidins far away.
8.7.9: Sterility, and infants’ death, and weeping that announceth woe, Dear! lay them on the fiend as thou wouldst pluck a garland from a tree. A charm to restore a sick man to health
8.8.1: The tawny-coloured, and the pale, the variegated and the red, The dusky-tinted, and the black,—all Plants we summon hither- ward.
8.8.10: This man let them deliver from Consumption which the Gods have sent. The father of these Herbs was Heaven, their mother Earth, the Sea their root.
8.8.11: The Waters are the best, and heavenly Plants. From every limb of thine have they removed Consumption caused by sin.
8.8.12: I speak to Healing Herbs spreading, and bushy, to creepers, and to those whose sheath is single, I call for thee the fibrous and the reed-like, and branching.
8.8.13: 131 Plants, dear to the Visve Devas, powerful, giving life to men.
8.8.14: The conquering strength, the power and might which ye, victo- rious Plants, possess, Therewith deliver this man here from this Consumption, O ye Plants: so I prepare the remedy.
8.8.15: The living Plant that giveth life, that driveth malady away, Arundhatr, the rescuer, strengthening, rich a sweets I call, to free this man from scath and
8.8.16: harm. Hitherward let the sapient come, the friendly sharers o f my speech. That we may give this man relief and raise him from his evil plight.
8.8.17: Germ of the Waters, Agni’s food, Plants ever growing fresh and new, Sure, healing, bearing thousand names, let them be all collected here.
8.8.18: Let Plants whose soul is water, girt with Avakās, piercing with their sharp horns expel the malady. Strong, antidotes of poison, those releasers, free from Varuna,
8.8.19: And those that drive away Catarrh, and those that frustrate magic arts, let all those Plants come hitherward.
8.8.2: Let purchased Plants of mightier power, Plants that are praised for excellence. Here in this village safely keep cattle and horses, man and beast. Sweet is their root, sweet are these Plants’ top branches, sweet also is their intermediate

8.8.21: Amrit: food, fatness let them yield, with kine preceding. These Plants that grow upon the earth, whate’er their number and their size, Let these with all their thousand leaves free me from Death and misery.
8.8.22: May the Plants’ Tiger-amulet, protective, guardian from the curse, Beat off the brood of demons, drive all maladies afar from us.
8.8.23: Before the gathered Plants they fly and scatter, as though a lion’s roar or fire dismayed them. Expelled by Plants, let men’s and kine’s Consumption pass from us to the navigable rivers. Emancipated from the sway of Agni, of Vaisvānara, go, covering the earth, ye Plants whose
8.8.24: ruler is Vanaspati. May these be pleasant to our heart, auspicious, rich in store of milk,
8.8.3: These Plants of the Angirases which grow on mountains and on plains. The Plants I know myself, the plants that with mine eye I look upon, Plants yet unknown, and those we know, wherein we find that power is stored,
8.8.4: Let all the congregated Plants attend and mark mine utterance, That we may rescue this man here and save him from severe distress.
8.8.5: Asvattha, Darbha, King of Plants, is Soma, deathless sacrifice Barley and Rice are healing balms, the sons of Heaven who never die. Lift yourselves up, ye Healing Plants, loud is the thunder’s crash and roar.
8.8.6: When with full flow Parjanya, ye Children of Prisni! blesseth; you. We give the essence of that stream of nectar of this man to drink:
8.8.7: So I prepare a remedy that he may live a hundred years. Well doth the wild boar know a Plant, the mungoose knows the Healing Herb.
8.8.8: I call, to aid this man, the Plants which Serpents and Gandhar- vas know. Plants of Angirases which hawks, celestial Plants which eagles. know;
8.8.9: Plants known to swans and lesser fowl, Plants known to all the birds that fly. Plants that are known to sylvan beasts,—I call them all to aid this man. The multitude of herbs whereon the Cows whom none may slaughter feed, all that are food
8.9.10: So many Plants, brought hitherward, give shelter and defence to thee! Hitherward unto thee I bring the Plants that cure all maladies, All Plants wherein physicians have discovered health-bestowing power.
8.9.11: Let Plants with flower and Plants with bud, the fruitful and the fruitless, all, Like children of one mother, yield their stores for this man’s perfeet health.
8.9.12: From the Five-arrowed, from the Ten-arrowed have I delivered thee, Freed thee from Yama’s fetter and from all offence against the Gods,
8.9.13: Imprecations directed against a hostile army Indra the Shaker shake them up, brave, hero, fortdemolisher,
8.9.14: That into thousand fragments we may strike the armies of our foes! Let Pūtirajju with her breath corrupt and putrefy that host, And terror smite our foemen’s heart when fire and smoke are seen afar.
8.9.15: Asvattha, rend those men; do thou devour them quickly, Khadira!
8.9.16: Like reeds let them be broken through, down-smitten by a lifted rush. Let Parushāhva make them reeds, and let the bulrush strike them down: Bound in a mighty net let them break quickly like an arrow’s shaft.
8.9.17: Air was the net; the poles thereof were the great quarters of the sky: Sakra therewith enveloped and cast on the ground the Dasyus’ host.
8.9.18: Verily mighty is the net of mighty Sakra rich in wealth: Therewith press all the foemen down so that not one of them escape! Great is thy net, brave Indra, thine the mighty match for a thousand, Lord of Hundred
8.9.19: Powers! Holding them, with his host, therewith hath Indra slaughtered
8.9.2: Dasyus a hundred, thousand, myriad, hundred millions. This world so mighty was the net of Sakra, of the Mighty One: With this, the net of Indra, I envelop all those men with gloom.
8.9.20: Great weakness and misfortune, pain which words can never charm away, Languor, fatigue, bewilderment, with these I compass all the foes.
8.9.21: I give those foemen up to Death: bound in the bonds of Death are they. I bind and carry them away to meet Death’s wicked messengers. Bear them away, Death’s messengers! envoys of Yama! bind them fast.
8.9.22: More than a thousand be their slain: the club of Bhava pierce them through! Forth go the Sādhyas in their might bearing one netpole raised aloft.
8.9.23: One pole the Rudras carry, one the Vasus, and the Ādityas one. The Visve Devas from above shall come depressing it with might, And in the midst the Angirases, slaying the mighty host, shall go.
8.9.24: Trees of the forest, trees that bear flower and fruit, and herbs and plants, Quadruped, biped send I forth that they may strike this army dead,
8.9.25: Gandharvas, and Apsarases, Gods, Serpents, Fathers, Holy Men, Seen and unseen, I send them forth that they may strike this army dead.
8.9.26: Here spread are snares of Death wherefrom thou, once within them, ne’er art freed: Full many a thousand of the host yonder this horn shall smite and slay.
8.9.3: The Gharma hath been warmed with fire: this Homa slays a thousand men. Let Bhava, Prisnibāhu, and Sarva destroy that armament. Their portion be the fire of Death, hunger, exhaustion, slaughter, fear.
8.9.4: 133 With your entangling snares and nets, Sarva and Indra! slay that host.
8.9.5: Fly, conquered, in alarm, ye foes, run driven by the spell away! Let not one man escape of those when routed by Brihaspati. Down fall their weapons on the ground: no strength be theirs to point a shaft:
