9.1.1: A glorification of the Asvins’ whip and a prayer for blessings The Asvins’ Honey-whip was born from heaven and earth, from middle air, and ocean, and
9.1.10: from fire and wind. All living creatures welcome it with joyful hearts, fraught with the store of Amrit it hath
9.1.11: gathered up. They call thee earth’s great strength in every form, they call thee too the ocean’s genial seed.
9.1.12: Whence comes the Honey-whip bestowing bounty, there Vital Spirit is, and Amrit treasured.
9.1.13: In sundry spots, repeatedly reflecting, men view upon the earth: her course and action; For she, the first-born daughter of the Maruts, derives her origin from Wind and Agni.
9.1.14: Daughter of Vasus, mother of Ādityas, centre of Amrit breath of living creatures. The Honey-whip, gold-coloured, dropping fatness, moves as a mighty embryo ‘mid mortals.
9.1.15: The deities begat the Whip of Honey: her embryo assumed all forms and fashions. The mother nourishes that tender infant which at its birth looks on all worlds and beings.
9.1.16: Who understandeth well, who hath perceived it, her heart’s un- injured Soma-holding beaker? Let the wise Brāhman priest therein be joyful.
9.1.17: He understandeth them, he hath perceived them, her breasts that pour a thousand streams, uninjured.
9.1.18: They unreluctantly yield strength and vigour. She who with voice upraised in constant clamour, mighty, life- giving, goes unto her
9.1.19: function, Bellowing to the heated three libations, suckles with streams of milk, and still is lowing.
9.1.2: On whom, well-fed, the Waters wait in worship, and steers and self-refulgent bulls attend her. For thee, for one like thee down pour the Waters, and cause desire and strength to rain upon
9.1.20: thee. The thunder is thy voice, O Lord of Creatures: a Bull, thou castest on the earth thy vigour.
9.1.21: The Honey-whip, the Manus’ first-born daughter, derives her origin from Wind and Agni. As at the morning sacrifice the Asvins twain love Soma well,
9.1.22: Even so may both the Asvins lay splendour and strength within my soul. As at the second sacrifice Indra and Agni love him well,
9.1.23: Let the pair, Indra Agni, lay splendour and strength within my soul. As at third sacrifice Soma is the Ribhus’ well-beloved one,
9.1.24: Even so may they, the Ribhus, store splendour and strength within my soul. Fain would I bring forth sweetness, fain would make it mine.
9.1.3: Bringing milk, Agni! have I come: splendour and strength bestow on me! Grant me, O Agni, splendid strength, and progeny, and length- ened life.
9.1.4: May the Gods know me as I am, may Indra with the Rishis know. As honey-bees collect and add fresh honey to their honey store,
9.1.5: Even so may both the Asvins lay splendour and strength within my soul. As over honey flies besmear this honey which the bees have made,
9.1.6: So may both Asvins lay in me splendour and strength and power and might. May all the sweetness that is found in hills and mountains, steeds and kine,
9.1.7: And wine that floweth from the cup,—may all that sweetness be in me. May both the Asvins, Lords of Light, balm me with honey of the bees,
9.1.8: 138 That I may speak among the folk words full of splendour and of strength.
9.1.9: The thunder is thy voice, O Lord of Creatures: a Bull, thou castest strength on earth and heaven.

9.9.5: The triplet with the two or four-foot measure, and with the syllable they form seven metres. With Jagatī the flood in heaven he stablished, and saw the Sun in the Rathantara Sāman. Gāyatri hath, they say, three logs for burning: hence it excels in majesty and vigour.

9.9.8: it. His mouth she fondly calls to her warm udder, and suckles him with milk while gently
9.9.9: lowing. He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow lows as she closely clings to him who sheds the rain.
9.10.1: She with her shrilling cries hath humbled mortal men, and turn- ed to lightning, hath stripped off her covering robe.
9.10.10: That which hath breath and life and speed and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses. The living moves by powers of the departed: the immortal is the brother of the mortal.
9.10.11: The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber, who runs his circling course with many round him.
9.10.12: Behold the God’s high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living. He who hath made him doth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely he is hidden.
9.10.13: He, yet enveloped in his mother’s bosom, source of much life, hath sunk into destruction. 150
9.10.14: I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing. He clothed with gathered and diffusive splendours, within the worlds continually travels. Dyaus is our father, our begetter: kinship is here. This great
9.10.15: Earth is our kin and mother. Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place. The
9.10.16: Father laid the Daughter’s germ within it. I bid thee tell me earth’s extremest limit, about the Stallion’s genial flow I ask thee; I ask about the universe’s centre, and touching highest heaven where Speech abideth.
9.10.17: The earth’s most distant limit is this altar: this Soma is the Stallion’s genial humour;
9.10.18: This sacrifice the universe’s centre: this Brāhman highest heaven where Speech abideth. What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander. When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this
9.10.19: Speech I first obtain a portion. Back, forward goes he, grasped by power inherent, immortal born the brother of the mortal.
9.10.2: Ceaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one and fail to mark the other. Seven germs unripened yet are Heaven’s prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Vishnu’s ordinance.
9.10.20: Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, present on every side they compass us about.
9.10.21: Upon what syllable of holy praise-hymn, as ‘twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-hymn? But they who know it well sit here
9.10.22: assembled. They, ordering the verse’s foot by measure, with the half-verse arranged each thing that
9.10.23: moveth. Prayer was diffused in many forms three-footed thereby the world’s four regions have their being

9.10.25: water. Forming the water-floods the Cow herself hath lowed, one-foot- ed or two-footed or four footed, she, Who hath become eight-footed or acquired nine feet, the uni- verse’s thousand-syllabled
9.10.26: Pankti. From her descend in streams the seas of water. Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured. Robed in the floods they fly aloft to heaven.

9.10.28: The Babe unborn supporteth this world’s burthen, supporteth Right and watcheth Wrong and Falsehood.
9.10.3: Virāj is Speech, and Earth, and Air’s mid-region. He is Praja- pati, and he is Mrityu. He is the Lord Imperial of the Sādhyas. He rules what is and what shall be hereafter. May he make me lord of what is and shall be.
9.10.4: I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it. The heroes cooked and dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days
9.10.5: aforetime. Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended.
9.10.6: One with his powers the universe regardeth. Of one the sweep is seen, but not the figure. 151
9.10.7: Speech hath been measured out in four divisions: the Brāhmans who have wisdom comprehend them. Three, kept in close concealment, cause no motion. Of Speech men speak the fourth division
9.10.8: only. They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni; and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān.
9.10.9: That which is One bards call by many a title: they call It Agni, Yama, Mātariswan. 152

10.6.11: Pure animating waters shall cleanse thee and make thee bright again. This Amulet, decked with chain of gold, shall give faith, sacrifice, and might, and dwell as
10.6.12: guest within our house. To this we give apportioned food, clarified butter, wine, and meath. May it provide each boon for us as doth a father for his sons.
10.6.13: Again, again, from morn to morn, having approached the deities. The Charm Brihaspati hath bound, the fatness-dropping citron- wood, the potent Khadira for
10.6.14: strength, This Agni hath put on: it yields clarified butter for this man. Again, again, from morn to morn. With this subdue thine enemies.
10.6.15: The Charm Brihaspati hath bound, the fatness-dropping citron- wood, the potent Khadira, for strength,
10.6.16: This Charm hath Indra put on him for power and manly puissance. It yieldeth strength to strengthen him, again, again, from morn to morn, having approached the deities.
10.6.17: The Charin Brihaspati, etc. This Charm hath Soma put on him for might, for hearing, and for sight.
10.6.18: This yields him energy indeed, again, again, etc. The Charm Brihaspati, etc. This Sūrya put on him, with this conquered the regions of the sky.
10.6.19: This yieldeth him ability, again, etc. The Charm Brihaspati, etc.
10.6.2: This Charm did Chandra wear, with this conquered the forts of Asuras, the golden forts of Dānavas. This yields him glory and renown, again, etc.
10.6.20: The Amulet Brihaspati bound on the swiftly-moving Wind. This yieldeth him a vigorous steed, again, etc.
10.6.21: The Asvins with this Amulet protect this culture of our fields. This yields the two Physicians might, again, etc. Savitar wore this Amulet: herewith he won this lucid heaven.
10.6.22: This yields him glory and delight, again, etc. Wearing this Charm the Waters flow eternally inviolate. This yieldeth them ambrosia, again
10.6.23: etc. King Varuna assumed and wore this salutary Amulet. This yieldeth him his truthfulness, again, etc.
10.6.24: Wearing this Amulet the Gods conquered in battle all the worlds. This yieldeth victory for them, again, etc.
10.6.25: The Amulet Brihaspati formed for the swiftly-moving Wind, This salutary Amulet the Deities assumed and wore. This yieldeth them the universe, again, again, from morn to morn. With this subdue thine
10.6.26: enemies. The seasons formed that Amulet, the Groups of Seasons fashion- ed it.
10.6.27: The Year having constructed it preserveth everything that is. The regions of the heaven, the points that lie between them fashioned it. Created by Prajāpati, may the Charm cast my foemen down.
10.6.28: 160 Atharvan made the Amulet, Atharvan’s children fashioned it.

10.7.15: Whitherward yearning blazeth Agni upward? Whitherward yearning bloweth Mātarisvan? Who out of many, tell me, is that Skambha to whom with long- ing go the turning pathways? Whitheward go the half-months, and, accordant with the full year, the months in their
10.7.16: procession? Who out of many, tell me, is that Skambha to whom go seasons and the groups of seasons?

10.7.2: future? That one part which he set in thousand places,—how far did

10.7.4: In the beginning, in the midst of the world, Skambha poured that gold. On Skambha Fervour rests, the worlds and Holy Law repose on him.
10.7.40: Skambha, I clearly know that all of thee on Indra is imposed. On Indra Fervour rests, on him the worlds and Holy Law recline. Indra, I clearly know that all of thee on Skambha findeth rest.

10.7.42: than which aught higher never hath arisen. Be reverence paid to him, that highest Brahma, whose base is Earth, his belly Air, who made the sky to be his head.

10.7.44: Agni for his mouth. Homage to highest Brahma, him whose two life-breathings were the Wind, The Angirases his sight: who made the regions be his means of sense.
10.7.5: Skambha set fast these two, the earth and heaven, Skambha maintained the ample air between them.
10.7.6: Skambha established the six spacious regions: this whole world Skambha entered and pervaded. Homage to highest Brahma, him who, sprung from Fervour and from toil,
10.7.7: Filled all the worlds completely, who made Soma for himself alone. Why doth the Wind move ceaselessly? Why doth the spirit take no rest?
10.7.8: Why do the Waters, seeking truth, never at any time repose? Absorbed in Fervour, is the mighty Being, in the world’s centre, on the waters’ surface. To him the Deities, one and all betake them. So stand the tree- trunk with the branches round
10.7.9: it. Who out of many, tell me, is that Skambha.
10.8.1: To whom the Deities with hands, with feet, and voice, and ear, and eye. Present unmeasured tribute in the measured hall of sacrifice? Darkness is chased away from him: he is exempt from all dist- ress.
10.8.10: In him are all the lights, the three abiding in Prajāpati. 163

10.8.12: weave it. The one draws out the threads, the other lays them: they break them not, they reach no end of
10.8.13: labour. Of these two, dancing round as ‘twere, I cannot distinguish whether ranks before the other. A Male in weaves this web, a Male divides it: a Male hath stretched it to the cope of heaven

10.8.15: Speculations on the Supreme Being and Cosmogonical and theological subjects Worship to loftiest Brahma, Lord of what hath been and what shall be, To him who rules the universe, and heavenly light is all his own!
10.8.16: Upheld by Skambha’s power these two, the heaven and the earth, stand fast. Skambha is all this world of life, whatever breathes or shuts an. eye.

10.8.18: understood it? Three hundred spokes have thereupon been hammered, and sixty pins set firmly in their
10.8.19: places. Discern thou this, O Savitar. Six are the twins, one singly born. They claim relationship in that among them which is born alone.
10.8.2: Though manifest, it lies concealed in the vast place they call the old: Therein is firmly stationed all the moving, breathing universe.
10.8.20: Up, eastward downward in the west, ‘it rolleth, with countless elements, one-wheeled, single fellied. With half it hath begotten all creation. Where hath the other half become unnoticed? In front of these the five-horsed car moves onward: side-horses, harnessed with the others
10.8.21: draw it. No one hath seen its hither course untravelled; the height sees it more near, the depth more
10.8.22: distant. The bowl with mouth inclined and bottom upward holds stored within it every form of glory. Thereon together sit the Seven Rishis who have become this mighty One’s protectors

10.8.26: These twain Heaven’s Lord divides as he advances, knowing the past hereof and all the future Within the womb Prajāpati is moving: he, though unseen, is born in sundry places. He with one half engendered all creation. What sign is there to tell us of the other?
10.8.27: All men behold him with the eye, but with the mind they know not him. Holding aloft the water as a water-bearer in her jar.
10.8.28: With the full vase he dwells afar, is left far off what time it fails, 164 A mighty Being in creation’s centre: to him the rulers of the realms bring tribute.
10.8.29: That, whence the Sun arises, that whither he goes to take his rest, That verily I hold supreme: naught in the world surpasses it.
10.8.3: Those who in recent times, midmost, or ancient, on all sides. greet the sage who knows the Veda, One and all, verily discuss Āditya, the second Agni, and the threefold Hansa.
10.8.30: This gold-hued Haiisa’s wings, flying to heaven, spread o’er a thousand days’ continued journey.
10.8.31: Supporting all the Gods upon his bosom, he goes his way behol- ding every creature. By truth he blazes up aloft by Brahma, he looks down below: He breathes obliquely with his breath, he on whom what is. highest rests.
10.8.32: The sage who knows the kindling-sticks whence by attrition wealth is drawn, Will comprehend what is most high, will know the mighty
10.8.33: Brāhmana. Footless at first was he produced, footless he brought celestial light. Four-footed grown, and meet for use, he seized each thing enjoyable.
10.8.34: Useful will he become, and then will he consume great store of food The man who humbly worshippeth the eternal and victorious
10.8.35: God. Him too they call eternal; he may become new again to-day. Day and Night reproduce themselves, each from the form the other wears.
10.8.36: A hundred, thousand, myriad, yea a hundred million stores of wealth that passes count are laid in him.
10.8.37: This wealth they kill as he looks on, and now this God shines bright therefrom. One is yet finer than a hair, one is not even visible. And hence the Deity who grasps with firmer hold is dear to me.
10.8.38: This fair one is untouched by age, immortal in a mortal’s house. He for whom she was made lies low, and he who formed her hath grown old.
10.8.39: Thou art a woman, and a man; thou art a damsel and a boy. Grown old thou totterest with a staff, new-born thou lookest every way. Either the sire or son of these, the eldest or the youngest child.
10.8.4: As sole God dwelling in the mind, first born, he still is in the womb. Forth from the full he lifts the full, the full he sprinkles with the full.

10.9.1: When Agni passed between the earth and heaven devouring with his flame the all-consumer, Where dwelt afar the spouses of one husband, where at that moment, where was Mātarisvan? Into the floods had Mātarisvan entered, the deities had past in- to the waters.
10.9.10: There stood the mighty measurer of the region: into the ver- dant plants went Pavamāna. Over the Gāyatri, above the immortal world he strode away.
10.9.11: Those who by Song discovered Song—where did the Unborn see that thing? Luller to rest, and gatherer-up of treasures, Savitar like a God whose laws are constant, hath stood like Indra in the war for riches.
10.9.12: Men versed in sacred knowledge know that living Being that abides. In the nine-portalled Lotus Flower, enclosed with triple bands and bonds.
10.9.13: Desireless, firm, immortal, self-existent, contented with the es- sence, lacking nothing, Free from the fear of Death is he who knoweth that Soul cou- rageous, youthful, undecaying. The Sataudanā or Hundredfold Oblation

10.9.15: Indra first gave the Hundredfold Oblation, welfare of him who worships, foe-destroying. Thy skin shall be the Altar; let thine hair become the Sacred Grass.

10.10.2: Cow With Kalis and Gandharvas by her side hath stepped upon the sea. Come hither with the Wind, yea, come with every creature borne on wings.

12.3.53: We have subdued that sinful-hearted Grāhi. Thou shalt speak sweetly having chased the darkness.
12.3.54: Let not the wooden gear made ready fail us, nor harm the grain of rice that pays due worship. Soon to be, decked with butter, all-embracing, come to this world wherewith birth unites thee.
12.3.55: Seize thou the winnowing-fan which rains have nourished, and let this separate the chaff and refuse.

12.3.59: mend it. Thou for thy son shalt yearn as yearns a mother. I lay thee down and with the earth unite thee.

12.4.16: Gods and Agnishtomas. Let thy fair form, wrought as by Tvashtar’s hatchet, mark these that yearn for thee within the vessel.
12.4.17: In sixty autumns may the Treasure-Guardian seek to gain heavenly light by cooked oblation. On this may sons and fathers live dependent. Send thou this mess to Fire that leads to heaven.
12.4.18: On the earth’s breast stand firmly as supporter: may Deities stir thee who ne’er hast shaken. So living man and wife with living children remove thee from the hearth of circling Agni. All wishes that have blessed those with fulfilment, having won all the worlds have met
12.4.19: together. Let them plunge in both stirring-spoon and ladle: raise this and set it in a single vessel.

12.4.20: extension. Herein be cooked the buffalo, strong-pinioned: the Gods shall give the Deities this oblation.
12.4.21: Whate’er thy wife, away from thee, makes ready, or what, O wife, apart from thee, thy husband, Combine it all: let it be yours in common while ye produce one world with joint endeavour.

12.4.25: The Lord of Treasures may desire this treasure: lordless on. every side be all the others. Our mess, presented seeking heaven, hath mounted in three divisions all three realms of Svarga.

12.5.1: He, Nārads! would know the Cow, then Brāhmans must be sought unto. Whoso calls her a worthless Cow, the stored-up treasure of the Gods,
12.5.10: Bhava and Sarva, both of them, move round and shoot a shaft at him. The man who hath no knowledge of her udder and the teats thereof,
12.5.11: She yields him milk with these, if he hath purposed to bestow the Cow. If he withholds the Cow they beg, she lies rebellious in his stall. Vain are the wishes and the hopes which he, withholding her, would gain.

12.5.20: Gods, Make manifest thy shape and form when she would seek her dwelling-place. Her shape and form she manifests when she would seek her dwelling-place;

12.5.22: Gods. Then verily the Brāhman priests approach that they may beg the Cow

12.5.3: But happy is the Cow when she is made a sacrifice to Gods. Nārada chose the terrible Vilipti out of all the cows Which the Gods formed and framed when they had risen up from sacri- fice

12.5.33: Homage, O Nārada, to thee who hast quick knowledge of the cows. Which of these is the direst, whose withholding bringeth death to man? Vilipti, O Brihaspati, cow, mother of no second calf—Of these none not a Brāhman should
12.5.34: eat if he hope for eminence. Threefold are kine, Vilipti, cow, the mother of no seeond calf:

12.5.39: They who seduce the owner of the Cow and say, Bestow her not. Encounter through their want of sense the missile shot by Rudra’s hand.
12.5.4: If in his home one cooks the Cow, sacrificed or not sacrificed. Wronger of Gods and Brāhmans’ he departs, dishonest, from the world.
12.5.40: On the duty of giving cows to Brāhmans, and the sin and danger of withholding the gift Created by toil and holy fervour, found by devotion, resting in right; Invested with truth, surrounded with honour, compassed about with glory;
12.5.41: Girt round with inherent power, fortified with faith, protected, by consecration, installed at sacrifice, the world her resting- place;
12.5.42: Brahma her guide, the Brāhman her lord and ruler; Of the Kshatriya who taketh to himself this Brāhman’s cow and oppresseth the Brāhman. The glory, the heroism, and the favouring fortune depart.

12.5.5: Running she is a thunderbolt, when driven away she is Vaisvā- nara; An arrow when she draweth up her hooves, and Mahādeva when she looketh around; Sharp as a razor when she beholdeth, she thundereth when she belloweth.
12.5.50: Death is she when she loweth, and a fierce God when she whis- keth her tail; Utter destruction when she moveth her ears this way and that,
12.5.51: Consumption when she droppeth water; A missile when milking, pain in the head when milked; The taking away of strength when she approacheth, a hand-to- hand fighter when roughly
12.5.52: touched; Wounding like an arrow when she is fastened by her mouth, contention when she is beaten;
12.5.53: Fearfully venomous when falling, darkness when she hath fallen down. Following him, the Brāhman’s cow extinguisheth the vital breath of the injurer of the Brāhman.

12.5.56: Sin while she is cooking, evil dream when she is cooked; Uprooting when she is being turned round, destruction when she hath been turned round;
12.5.57: Discord by her smell, grief when she is being eviscerated: ser- pent with poison in its fang when drawn; Loss of power while sacrificially presented, humiliation when she hath been offered;

12.5.6: a secret spell. Homelessness is she when denied her rights.

13.1.1: The glorification of Rohita, a form of Fire and of the Sun Rise, Mighty One, who liest in the waters, and enter this thy fair and glorious kingdom.
13.1.10: Let Rohita who made this All uphold thee carefully nurtured for supreme dominion. The strength that was in waters hath ascended. Mount o’er the tribes which thou hast
13.1.11: generated. Creating Soma, waters, plants and cattle, bring hitherward both quadrupeds and bipeds.
13.1.12: Ye Maruts, strong and mighty, sons of Prisni, with Indra for ally crush down our foemen. Let Rohita, ye bounteous givers, hear you, thrice-seven Maruts who delight in sweetness!
13.1.13: Up to the lap of births, to lofty places, hath Rohita, the germ of Dames, ascended. Conjoined with these he found the six realms: seeing his way in front here he received the
13.1.14: kingship. For thee hath Rohita obtained dominion, scattered thine ene- mies, become thy safeguard.
13.1.15: So by the potent Sakvaris let Heaven and Earth be milked to- yield thee all thy wishes. Rohita gave the Earth and Heavens their being. There Para- meshthin held the cord extended.
13.1.16: Thereon reposeth Aja Ekapāda. He with his might hath stab- lished Earth and Heaven. Rohita firmly stablished Earth and Heaven: by him was ether fixt by him the welkin.
13.1.17: He measured out mid air and all the regions: by him the Gods found life that lasts for ever. Arranging shoots, springs, Rohita considered this Universe in all its forms and phases.
13.1.18: May he, gone up to heaven with mighty glory, anoint thy sov- ranty with milk and fatness. Thy risings up, thy mountings and ascensions wherewith thou fillest heaven and air’s mid region—
13.1.19: By prayer for these, by milk of these, increasing, in Rohita’s kingdom watch, among his people.
13.1.2: The tribes thy heat produced have followed hither the Calf and Gāyatri, the strain that lauds him.
13.1.20: With friendly heart let them approach to serve thee, and the Calf Rohita come with his mother.
13.1.21: Erected, Rohita hath reached the welkin, wise, young, creating every form and figure. Agni, refulgent with his heightened lustre, in the third realm hath brought us joy and
13.1.22: gladness. Thousand-horned Bull, may Jātavedas, worshipped with butter, balmed with Soma, rich in
13.1.23: heroes, Besought, ne’er quit me; may I ne’er forsake thee. Give me abundant men and herds of cattle.
13.1.24: Rohita is the sire and mouth of worship: to him with voice, ear, heart I pay oblation. To Rohita come Gods with joyful spirit. May he by risings raise me till I join him.
13.1.25: Rohita ordered sacrifice for Visvakarman: thence have I obta- ined this strength and energy. May I proclaim thee as my kin over the greatness of the world.
13.1.26: On thee have mounted Brihatī and Pankti. and Kakup with great splendour, Jātavedas! The cry of Vashat with the voice uplifted and Rohita with seed on thee have mounted.
13.1.27: He goes into the womb of earth, he robes himself in heaven and air. He on the Bright One’s station hath reached heavenly light and all the worlds.
13.1.28: To us, Vāchaspati, may Earth be pleasant, pleasant our dwelling, pleasant be our couches. Even here may Prāna be our friend: may Agni, O Parameshthin give thee life and splendour.
13.1.29: And those, Vāchaspati, our own five seasons, sacred to Visva- karman their creator. 200
13.1.3: Even here our friend be Prāna: Parameshthin, may Rohita vouchsafe the life and splendour. Breed, O Vāchaspati, joy and understanding, kine i n our stall and children in our consorts.
13.1.30: Even here may Prāna be our friend: may Agni, O Parameshthin, give thee life and splendour. With splendour let God Savitar, and Agni, with splendour
13.1.31: Mitra, Varuna invest thee. Treading down all Malignities, come hither. Pleasant and’ glorious hast thou made this
13.1.32: kingdom. Rohita, car-borne by a speckled leader, thou, pouring water,. goest on in triumph.
13.1.33: Golden, refulgent, lofty is the Lady, Rohinī, Rohita’s devoted Consort.
13.1.34: Through her may we win various spoil and booty, through her be conquerors in every battle. Rohita’s seat is Rohinī before us: that is the path the speckled
13.1.35: Mare pursueth. Kasyapas and Gandharvas lead her upward, and heavenly sages ever watch and guard her,
13.1.36: Sūrya’s bay steeds refulgent and immortal draw the light-rolling. chariot on for ever. Drinker of fatness, Rohita, resplendent, hath entered into various-coloured heaven,
13.1.37: Rohita, Bull whose horns are sharply pointed, superior of Agni and of Sūrya, He who supports the sundered earth and heaven,—from him the
13.1.38: Gods effect their own creations. Rohita rose to heaven from mighty ocean, Rohita rose and clomb all steeps and rises.
13.1.39: Prepare the Milky One who teems with fatness: she is the Gods’ never-reluctant milch-cow. Indra drink Soma: ours be peace and safety. Let Agni lead the laud, and chase our foemen.
13.1.4: Both kindling and inflamed, adored with butter and enhanced thereby. May conquering Agni, conqueror of all, destroy mine enemies.
13.1.40: Let him smite down in death and burn the foeman who attacketh me. Our adversaries we consume through Agni the Carnivorous.
13.1.41: Beat them down, Indra, with thy bolt, beat them down, mighty with thine arm. I through the energy and force of Agni have secured my foes.
13.1.42: Cast down our foes beneath our feet, O Agni. Brihaspati, oppress our rebel kinsman. Low let them fall, O Indra-Agni. Mitra-Varuna, powerless to show their anger.
13.1.43: Ascending up on high, O God. O Sūrya, drive my foes away. Yea, beat them backward with the stone: to deepest darkness let them go.
13.1.44: Calf of Virāj, the Bull of prayers and worship, whitebacked, he hath gone up to air’s mid region. Singing, they hymn the Calf, with gifts of butter: him who is
13.1.45: Brahma they exalt with Brahma. Rise up to earth, rise up to heaven above it; rise up to opulence, rise up to kingship.
13.1.46: Rise up to offspring, rise to life immortal; rise, and with Rohita unite thy body. With all the Gods who circle round the Sun, upholding royal sway,
13.1.47: With all of these may Rohita accordant, give sovranty to thee with friendly spirit. Cleansed by prayer, sacrifices bear thee upward: bay coursers, ever travelling, convey thee.
13.1.48: Thy light shines over sea and billowy ocean. Rohita, conqueror of cows and riches and gathered spoil, is heaven’s and earth’s upholder.
13.1.49: Over earth’s greatness would I tell my kinship with thee who hast a thousand births and seven.
13.1.5: A glorious sight to beasts and men, thou goest glorious to the regions and mid-regions. On earth’s, on Aditi’s bosom, bright with glory. Fain would I equal Savitar in beauty.
13.1.50: Thou, yonder, knowest all things here, when here thou knowest what is there. From here men see the sphere of light, Sūrya profoundly wise in heaven.
13.1.51: A God, thou injurest the Gods: thou movest in the ocean’s depth. 201
13.1.52: Men kindle common Agni: him only the higher sages know. Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her Calf at foot, the Cow hath risen
13.1.53: Whitherward, to what place hath she departed? Where doth she calve? Not in this herd of cattle.
13.1.54: She hath become one-footed or two-footed, four-footed, or eight-footed or nine-footed, This universe’s thousand-syllabled Pankti Oceans flow forth from her in all directions.
13.1.55: Rising to heaven, immortal, hear my calling. Cleansed by prayer, sacrifices bear thee upward. Bay coursers, ever on the road, convey thee.
13.1.56: This, O Immortal One, I know of thee, thy progress to the sky thy dwelling-place in loftiest heaven.
13.1.57: Beyond the sky, beyond the Earth looks Sūrya, and beyond the floods. The single eye of all that is; to mighty heaven hath he arisen.
13.1.58: The earth was made his altar, and the wide expanses were the fence. There Rohita established both these Agnis, fervent heat and cold.
13.1.59: He stablished heat and cold, he made the mountains sacrificial posts. Then both the Agnis, Rohita’s who found celestial light, with rain for molten butter,
13.1.6: sacrificed. Rohita’s Agni-his who found heaven’s light-is kindled with the prayer.
13.1.60: From him the heat, from him the cold, from him the sacrifice was born. Both Agins-Rohita’s who found the light of heaven—made strong by prayer,
13.1.7: Waxing by prayer, adored with prayer, by prayer enkindled, sacrificed. One is deposited in Truth, one kindled in the waters: both
13.1.8: Agnis of Rohita who found the light are set aflame with prayer. That decked by Wind, and that prepared by Indra Brāhman- aspati,
13.1.9: Agnis of Rohita who found light, prayer-enkindled, sacrificed. Rohita made the earth to be his altar, heaven his Dakshinā.
13.2.1: Then heat he took for Agni, and with rain for molten butter he created every living thing. The earth became an altar, heat was Agni, and the butter rain.
13.2.10: There Agni made, by song and hymn, these mountains rise and stand erect. Then, having made the hills stand up, Rohita spake to Earth, and said:
13.2.11: In thee let every thing be born, what is and what is yet to be. This sacrifice, the first of all, the past, the present, had its birth.
13.2.12: From that arose this universe, yea, all this world of brightness, brought by Rohita the heavenly Sage.
13.2.13: If thou should kick a cow, or by indecent act offend the Sun, Thy root I sever; nevermore mayst thou cast shadow on the ground.
13.2.14: Thou who, between the fire and me, passest across the line of shade. Thy root I sever: nevermore mayst thou cast shadow on the ground.
13.2.15: Whoe’er he be who, Sūrya, God! comes between thee and me to-day, On him we wipe away ill-dream, and troubles, and impurity.
13.2.16: Let us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser’s sacrifice. Let not malignities dwell with us.
13.2.17: May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out tc reach the Gods, That perfecteth our sacrifice.
13.2.18: The glorification of the Sun as Āditya, Sūrya and Rohita Radiant, refulgent in the sky are reared the banners of his light,
13.2.19: Āditya’s, who beholdeth man, mighty in act and bountiful. Let us laud him, the whole world’s Herdsman, Sūrya, who with his rays illumines all the
13.2.20: Mark of the quarters, brightening them with lustre, swift, mighty-pinioned, flying in the ocean.
13.2.21: From west to east thou speedest freely, making by magic day and night of diverse colours. This is Āditya, thy transcendent glory, that thou alone art born through all creation.
13.2.22: Victorious, inspired, and brightly shining, whom seven strong tawny-coloured coursers carry, Whom Atri lifted from the flood to heaven, thus men behold thee as thy course thou runnest.
13.2.23: Let them not snare thee speeding on thy journey: pass safely, swiftly places hard to traverse, While measuring out the day and night thou movest—O Sūrya, even Heaven and Earth the
13.2.24: Goddess. Hail to thy rapid car whereon, O Sūrya, thou circlest in a moment both the limits,
13.2.25: Whirled by thy bay steeds, best of all at drawing, thy hundred horses or seven goodly coursers!
13.2.26: Mount thy strong car, O Sūrya, lightly rolling, drawn by good steeds, propitious, brightly gleaming,
13.2.27: Whirled by thy bays, most excellent at drawing, thy hundred horses or seven goodly coursers. Sūrya hath harnessed to his car to draw him seven stately bay steeds gay with wolden
13.2.28: housings. The Bright One started from the distant region: dispelling gloom the God hath climbed the
13.2.29: heavens. With lofty banner hath the God gone upward, and introduced the light, expelling darkness.
13.2.3: He hath looked round on all the worlds, the Hero, the son of Aditi, Celestial Eagle.
13.2.30: Rising, thou spreadest out thy rays, thou nourishest all shapes and forms. Thou with thy power illumest both the oceans, encompassing all spheres with thy refulgence.
13.2.31: Moving by magic power to east and westward, these two young creatures, sporting, circle ocean.
13.2.32: One of the pair beholds all living creatures: with wheels of gold the bay steeds bear the other. Atri established thee in heaven. O Surya, to create the month.
13.2.33: So on thou goest, firmly held, heating, beholding all that is. As the Calf both his parents so thou joinest both the distant bounds,
13.2.34: Surely the Gods up yonder knew this sacred mystery long ago. Sūrya is eager to obtain all wealth that lies along the sea,
13.2.35: Great is the course spread out for him, his eastward and his westward path. He finishes his race with speed and never turns his thought aside,
13.2.36: Thereby he keeps not from the Gods enjoyment of the Drink of Life. His heralds bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that live,
13.2.37: Sūrya, that all may look on him. The Constellations pass away, like thieves, departing in the night.
13.2.38: Before the all-beholding Sun. His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o’er the world of men, Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
13.2.39: Swift and all-beautiful art thou, O Sūrya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
13.2.4: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind, Hither, all light to behold. With that same eye of thine wherewith thou seest, brilliant
13.2.40: Varuna. The active one among mankind,
13.2.41: 203 Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days, Sun, seeing all things that have life.
13.2.42: Seven bay steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou far- seeing One, God, Sūrya, with the radiant hair.
13.2.43: Sūrya, hath yoked the pure bright seven, the daughters of the car, with these, His own dear team, he travelleth. Devout, aflame with fervent heat, Rohita hath gone up to heaven.
13.2.44: He is re-born, returning to his birthplace, and hath become the Gods’ imperial ruler.
13.2.45: Dear unto all men, facing all directions, with hands and palms on every side extended, He, the sole God, engendering earth and heaven, beareth them with his wings and arms together.
13.2.46: The single-footed hath outstepped the biped, the biped overtakes the triple-footed. The biped hath outstridden the six-footed: these sit around the single-footed’s body.
13.2.5: When he, unwearied, fain to go, hath mounted his bays, he makes two colours, brightly shining. Rising with banners, conquering the regions, thou sendest light through all the floods, Āditya.
13.2.6: Verily, Sūrya, thou art great: truly, Āditya, thou art great. Great is thy grandeur, Mighty One: thou, O Āditya, thou art great.
13.2.7: In heaven, O Bird, and in mid-air thou shinest: thou shinest on the earth and in the waters. Thou hast pervaded both the seas with splendour: a God art thou, O God, light-winner, mighty.
13.2.8: Soaring in mid-course hither from the distance, fleet and ins- pired, the Bird that flies above us,
13.2.9: With might advancing Vishnu manifested, he conquers all that moves with radiant banner: Brilliant, observant, mighty Lord, an Eagle illuming both the spheres and air between them. Day and the Night, clad in the robes of Sūrya, spread forth more widely all his hero powers.
13.3.1: Flaming and radiant, strengthening his body, bestowing floods that promptly come to meet us,
13.3.10: He, luminous, winged, mighty, strength-bestower, hath mounted all the regions as he forms them. Bright presence of the Gods, the luminous herald Sūrya hath mounted the celestial regions.
13.3.11: Day’s maker, he hath shone away the darkness, and radiant, passed o’er places hard to traverse.
13.3.12: He hath gone up on high, the Gods’ bright presence, the eye of Mitra, Varuna and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, Sūrya hath filled the earth and air and heaven,
13.3.13: High in the midst of heaven may we behold thee whom men call Savitar, the bright red Eagle,
13.3.14: Soaring and speeding on thy way, refulgent, unwasting light which Atri erst discovered. Him, Son of Aditi, an Eagle hasting along heaven’s height, I supplicate in terror, As such prolong our lengthened life, O Sūrya: may we, unha- rmed, enjoy thy gracious
13.3.15: favour. This gold-hued Hansa’s wings, soaring to heaven, spread o’er a thousand days’ continued
13.3.16: journey Supporting all the Gods upon his bosom, he goes his way behold- ing every creature. Rohita, in primeval days Prajāpati, was, after, Time, Mouth of all sacrifices, he, Rohita,
13.3.17: brought celestial light. He, Rohita, became the world: Rohita gave the heaven its heat.
13.3.18: Rohita with his beams of light travelled along the earth and sea. 204 To all the regions Rohita came, the imperial Lord of heaven.
13.3.19: He watches over ocean, heaven, and earth and all existing things. Mounting the lofty ones, he, bright, unwearied, splendidly shining, makes two separate
13.3.2: colours, While through all worlds that are he sends his lustre, radiant, observant, mighty, wind approacher. One form comes on, the other is reverted: to day and night the
13.3.20: Strong One shapes and fits him. With humble prayer for aid we call on Sūrya, who knows the way, whose home is in the
13.3.21: region. The suppliant’s way, filling the earth, the Mighty circleth the world with eye that none deceiveth.
13.3.22: May he, all-seeing, well-disposed and holy, give ear and listen to the word I utter. Blazing with light his majesty hath compassed ocean and earth and heaven and air’s mid region.
13.3.23: May he, all-seeing, well-disposed and holy, give ear and listen to the word I utter. Agni is weakened by the people’s fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow, Like young trees shooting up on high their branches, his flames are mounting to the vault of
13.3.24: heaven. A glorification of Rohita. with a malediction on the man who wrongs a Brāhman
13.3.25: He who engendered these, the earth and heaven, who made the worlds the mantle that he weareth, In whom abide the six wide-spreading regions through which the
13.3.26: Bird’s keen vision penetrateth, This God is wroth offended by the sinner who wrongs the
13.3.3: Brāhman who hath gained this knowledge Agitate him, O Rohita; destroy him: entangle in thy snares the Brāman’s tyrant.
13.3.4: He from whom winds blow pure in ordered season, from whom the seas flow forth in all directions,
13.3.5: This God, etc. He who takes life away, he who bestows it; from whom comes breath to every living creature,
13.3.6: This God, etc. Who with the breath he draws sates earth and heaven, with expiration fills the ocean’s belly,
13.3.7: This God, etc. In whom Virāj, Prajāpati, Parameshthin, Agni Vaisvānara abide with Pankti, He who hath taken to himself the breathing of the Supreme, the vigour of the Highest,
13.3.8: This God, etc. On whom rest six expenses and five regions, four waters, and three syllables of worship,
13.3.9: He who hath looked between both spheres in anger, This God, etc. He who, consuming food, became its master, the Lord of Prayer, the Regent of Devotion,
13.4.1: The world’s Lord, present and to be hereafter, This God, etc.
13.4.10: He who metes out the thirteenth month, constructed with days and nights, containing thirty members, This God, etc.
13.4.11: 205 Dark the descent; the strong-winged birds are golden: they fly aloft to heaven, enrobed in
13.4.12: waters. They have come hither from the seat of Order, This God, etc.
13.4.13: What silver. Kasyapa, thou hast refulgent, what brightly-shining lotus-flower collected, Wherein are gathered seven Suns together,
13.4.2: This God, etc. In front the Brihat-Sāman is his mantle, and from behind Rathantara enfolds him,
13.4.3: Ever with care robing themselves in splendour. This God, etc.
13.4.4: One of his wings was Brihat, and the other Rathantarr., vigorous with one same purpose, What time the Gods gave Rohita his being. This God, etc.
13.4.5: At evening he is Varuna and Agni, ascending in the morning he is Mitra. As Savitar, he moves through air’s mid region, as Indra warms- the heavens from the centre.
13.4.6: This God, etc. This gold-hued Harisa’s wings, soaring to heaven spread o’er a thousand days’ continued journey.
13.4.7: Supporting all the Gods upon his bosom, he goes his way behol- ding every creature. This God, etc.
13.4.8: This is the God who dwells-within the waters, the thousand- rooted, many-powered Atri, He who brought all this world into existence. This God; etc.
13.4.9: With flying feet his tawny coursers carry the bright God through, the sky, aglow with splendour.
13.5.14: Whose limbs uplifted fire and heat the heavens: hither he shines- with beams of golden colour. This God, etc.
13.5.15: He beside whom his bay steeds bear the Ādityas, by whom as sacrifice go many knowing. The sole light shining spread through various places.
13.5.16: This God, etc. This seven make the one-wheeled chariot ready: bearing seven names the single courser draws it.
13.5.17: The wheel, three-naved, is sound and undecaying: thereon these worlds of life are all dependent.
13.5.18: This God, etc. Eight times attached the potent Courser draws it, Sire of the Gods, father of hymns and praises.
13.5.19: So Mātarisvan, measuring in spirit the thread of Order, purifies all regions. This God, etc.
13.5.20: The thread that goes through all celestial quarters within the Gāyatri, womb of life eternal. This God, etc.
13.5.21: There are the settings, three the upward risings, three are the- spaces, yea, and three the heavens.
13.6.22: We know thy triple place of birth, O Agni, we know the deities’’ triple generations. He who, as soon as born, laid broad earth open, and set the ocean in the air’s mid-region, This God, etc.
13.6.23: Thou, Agni, kind with lights and mental powers, hast up in heaven shone as the Sun, 206
13.6.24: enkindled. The Maruts, sons of Prisni, sang his praises what time the Gods gave Rohita his being. This God, etc.
13.6.25: Giver of breath, giver of strength and vigour, he whose com- mandment all the Gods acknowledge,
13.6.26: He who is Lord of this, of man and cattle, This God, etc. The single-footed hath outstepped the biped, the biped overtakes the triple-footed. The quadruped hath wrought when bipeds called him, standing and looking on the five
13.6.27: collected. This God is wroth offended by the sinner that wrongs the
13.6.28: Brāhman who hath gained this knowledge. Agitate him, O Rohita; destroy him: entangle in thy snares the Brāhman’s tyrant.
13.7.29: Born is the darksome Mother’s Son, the whitely shining Calf of Night.
13.7.30: He, Rohita, ascendeth up to heaven, hath mounted to the heights. A glorification of the Sun as the only Deity Down looking, on the ridge of sky Savitar goes to highest heaven.
13.7.31: To misty cloud filled with his rays Mahendra goes encompassed round. Creator and Ordainer, he is Vāyu, he is lifted cloud.
13.7.32: Rudra, and Mahādeva, he is Aryaman and Varuna. Agni is he, and Siirya, he is verily Mahāyama. Calves, joined, stand close beside him, ten in number, with one single head.
13.7.33: From west to east they bend their way: when he mounts up he shines afar. His are these banded Maruts: they move gathered close like porters’ thongs.
13.7.34: To misty cloud filled with his rays Mahendra goes encompassed round, His are the nine supports, the casks set in nine several places here. He keeppeth watch o’er creatures, all that breatheth and that breatheth not.
13.7.35: This conquering might hath entered him, He is the sole the simple One, the One alone. In him these Deities become simple and One
13.7.36: Renown and glory, and force and cloud, the Brāhman’s splendour, and food, and nourishment, To him who knoweth this God as simple and one.
13.7.37: Neither second, nor third, nor yet fourth is he called; He is called neither fifth, nor sixth, nor yet seventh
13.7.38: He is called neither eighth, nor ninth, nor yet tenth. He watcheth over creatures, all that breatheth and that breatheth not. This conquering might hath entered him. He is the sole, the simple One, the One alone,
13.7.39: In him these Deities become simple and One Devotion and Religious Fervour, and renown and glory, and force and cloud, the Brāhman’s
13.7.40: splendour, and food and nourishment. And past and future, and Faith and lustre, and heaven and sweet oblation, To him who knoweth this God as simple and One.
13.7.41: He, verily, is death, he is immortality, he is the monster, he is the fiend. He is Rudra, winner of wealth in the giving of wealth; in uttering homage he is the sacrificial
13.7.42: exclamation Vashat duly employed. All sorcerers on earth obey with reverence his high behest. All constellations yonder, with the Moon, are subject to his will.
13.7.43: 207 He was brought forth from Day: and Day derives his origin. from him.
13.7.44: He was brought forth from Night: and Night derives her origins from him. He was produced from Air: and Air derives its origin from him. He was produced from Wind: and Wind derives his origin from. him.
13.7.45: From Heaven was he produced: and Heaven derives his origin from him. He sprang from regions of the sky: from him the heavenly regions sprang.
13.8.46: He is the offspring of the Earth: Earth hath her origin from him. He was produced from fire: and fire derives its origin from him. He is the waters’ offspring: and from him the waters were produced.
13.8.47: From holy verses was he born: from him the holy verses sprang. He is the son of sacrifice: and sacrifice was born from him.
13.8.48: Sacrifice, sacrifice’s Lord, he was made head of sacrifice. He thundereth, he lighteneth, he casteth down the thunder-stone For misery or happiness, for mortal man or Asura.
13.8.49: Whether thou formest growing plants, or sendest rain for happiness, or hast increased the race of man,
13.8.50: Such is thy greatness, liberal Lord! A hundred bodily forms are thine. Millions are in thy million, or thou art a billion in thyself. Stronger than immortality is Indra: stronger thou than deaths;
13.8.51: Yea, stronger than Malignity art thou, O Indra, Lord of Might. Calling thee Master, Sovran Chief, we pay our reverence to thee.
13.9.52: Worship to thee whom all behold! Regard me, thou whom all regard, With food, and fame, and vigour, with the splendour of a Brāhman’s rank
13.9.53: We pay thee reverence calling thee strength, power, and might, and conquering force. We pay thee reverence calling thee red power, the silvery expanse.
13.9.54: We pay thee reverence calling thee vast, wide, the good, the universe. We pay thee reverence, calling thee extension, compass, width, and world. We pay thee reverence, calling thee rich, opulent in this and that, with wealth unceasing and
13.9.55: secure Worship to thee whom all behold! Regard me, thou whom all regard.
13.9.56: With food, and fame, and vigour, with the splendour of a Brāhman’s rank. 208

14.1.1: On the Bridal of Sūryā, marriage ceremonies in general Truth is the base that bears the earth; by Sūrya are the heavens upheld.
14.1.10: By Law the Ādityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven. By Soma are the Ādityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth:
14.1.11: Thus Soma in the lap of all these constellations hath his home. One thinks, when men have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma’s juice.
14.1.12: Of him whom Brāhmans truly know as Soma never mortal eats. When they begin to drink thee, then, O God, thou swellest out again.

18.2.1: Yes, this is good to taste and full of sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour. No one may conquer Indra in the battle when he hath drunken of the draught we offer.
18.2.10: Honour the King with your oblations, Yama, Vivasvān’s son, who gathers men together. Even him who travelled o’er the mighty rivers, who searches out and shows the path to many. Yama first found for us the road to travel: this pasture never can be taken from us.
18.2.11: Men born on earth tread their own paths that lead them whither our ancient Fathers have departed.
18.2.12: Fathers who sit on sacred grass, come, help us: these offsprings have we made for you; accept them. So come to us with most auspicious favour: bestow on us unfailing health and plenty.
18.2.13: Bowing their bended knees and seated southward let all accept this sacrifice with favour. 231
18.2.14: Punish us not for any sin, O fathers which we through human frailty have committed. Tvashtar prepares the bridal for his daughter: therefore the whole of this our world assembles. But Yama’s mother, spouse of great Vivasvān, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling.
18.2.15: Go forth, go forth upon the homeward pathways whither our sires of old have gone before us. Then shalt thou look on both the Kings enjoying their sacred food, God Varuna and Yama.
18.2.16: Go hence, depart ye, fly in all directions. This world for him the Fathers have provided. Yama bestow upon this man a dwelling adorned with days and beams of light and waters.
18.2.17: We set thee down with yearning, and with yearning we enkindle thee, Yearning, bring yearning Fathers nigh to eat the food of sacrifice.
18.2.18: We, splendid men, deposit thee, we, splendid men, enkindle thee. Splendid, bring splendid Fathers nigh to eat the sacrificial food. Our Fathers are Angirases, Navagvas, Atharvans, Bhrigus, who deserve the Soma.
18.2.19: May these, the holy, look on us with favour; may we enjoy their gracious loving-kindness. Come, Yama, with Angirases, the holy; rejoice thee here with children of Virūpa.
18.2.2: Seated on sacred grass at this oblation: I call Vivasvān too, thy father, hither. Come, seat thee on this bed of grass. O Yama, accordant with Angirases and Fathers.
18.2.20: Let texts recited by the sages bring thee. O. King, let this oblation make thee joyful. He hath gone hence and risen on high mounting heaven’s ridges by that path
18.2.21: Whereon the sons of Angiras, the conquerors of earth, went up. A funeral hymn, taken mainly from the Rigveda For Yama Soma juice flows clear, to Yama is oblation paid.
18.2.22: To Yama sacrifice prepared, and heralded by Agni, goes. Offer to Yama sacrifice most sweet in savour and draw near.
18.2.23: Bow down before the Rishis of the olden time, the ancient ones who made the path. Offer to Yama, to the King, butter and milk in sacrifice. So may he grant that we may live long days of life mid living men,
18.2.24: Burn him not up, nor quite consume him, Agni. Let not his body or his skin be scattered. O Jātavedas, when thou hast matured him, then send him on his way unto the Fathers.
18.2.25: When thou hast made him ready, Jātavedas, then do thou give him over to the Fathers. When he attains unto the life that waits him he will obey the Deities’ commandment.
18.2.26: With the three jars Brihat alone makes pure the six wide-spread- ing realms. The Gāyatri, the Trishtup, all metres in Yama are contained.
18.2.27: The Sun receive thine eye, the wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven. Go, if it be thy lot, unto the waters: go, make thy home in plants with all thy members. Thy portion is the goat: with heat consume him: let thy fierce flame, thy glowing splendour,
18.2.28: burn him. With thine auspicious forms, O Jātavedas, bear this man to the region of the pious.
18.2.29: Let all thy rapid flames, O Jātavedas, wherewith thou fillest heaven and earth’s mid-region, Follow the goat as he goes on, united: then with the others, most auspicious, aid us. 1Away O Agni, to the Fathers, send him who, offered in thee, goes with our oblations.

18.2.4: Unite thee with the Fathers and with Yama: strong and delicious be the winds that fan thee. Floating in water, bringing streams, let Maruts carry thee aloft, And causing coolness by their rush sprinkle thee with their fall- ing rain.
18.2.40: I have recalled thy life to life, to being, power, and energy. Let thy soul go unto its own: so to the Fathers hasten thou.

18.2.42: Among the Fathers find thy home, and thrive mid those whom Yama rules.
