19.40.1: Thither let Agni lead me, let Agni give me intelligence, All hail to Agni! Whither etc. Thither let Vāyu lead me, let Vāyu vouchsafe me vital breath.
19.40.2: All hail to Vāyu! Whither, etc.
19.40.3: Thither let Sūrya lead me, let Sūrya vouchsafe me power of sight. All hail to Sürya Whither, etc. Thither let Chandra lead me, let Chandra vouchsafe me intellect.
19.40.4: All hail to Chandra! Whither, etc.
19.41.1: Thither let Soma lead me, let Soma vouchsafe me vital sap. All hail to Soma! Whither, etc. Thither let Indra lead me, let Indra bestow upon me power. All hail to Indra!
19.42.1: Whither, etc. Thither, let Waters lead me, let the Waters give me deathless life. All hail to Waters!
19.42.2: Whither, etc. Thither let Brahma lead me, let Brahma give Brahma unto me. All hail to Brahma!
19.42.3: A curative and protective charm Thou art the lengthening of life, thy name is Universal Cure:
19.42.4: Then, Ointment! send felicity; Waters, send happiness and peace. The yellow hue, the feverish heat, the shooting pain that rends II the limbs, All the consumptive malady let the Ointment drive from out thy frame.
19.43.1: 258 Let the Salve born upon the earth, benignant, giving life to man.
19.43.2: Make the swift rider on the car sinless, exempt from sudden death. Preserve our breath, O Vital Breath, have mercy on our life, O Life.
19.43.3: From snares of Nirriti do thou, O Nirriti, deliver us. Thou art the babe of Sindhu, thou art lightnings’ flower, wind, breath, and Sun: thou art the
19.43.4: eye and milk of heaven. Gods’ Ointment from the Three Peaked Hill, preserve thou me on every side. No plants of earth surpass thee, none from mountain or from cultured ground.
19.43.5: Now hath it gently crept within, fiend-slaying, chasing malady. And driving all diseases hence, and evil omens, banished them.
19.43.6: Full many a falsehood, O thou King Varuna, man hath uttered here: Do thou who hast a thousand powers preserve us from that misery. If we have cried, O Waters! Cows! if we have cried, O
19.43.7: Varuna! For this endowed with thousand powers! deliver us from misery.
19.43.8: Mitra and Varuna, O Salve have closely followed after thee May they, when they have followed thee afar, restore thee for our use. A curative and protective charm
19.44.1: As debt from debt repay and send sorcery to the sorcerer’s house. Split, Salve! the cruel villain’s ribs whose evil eye bewitches us.
19.44.10: Whatever evil dream we have, what’er befall our kine or home, Be this that is salubrity, the evil-hearted’s foe applied. Increasing from the Waters’ strength and vigour, sprung into life from Agni Jātavedas,
19.44.2: Strong as four heroes, mountain born, this Ointment make for thee quarters and mind-points auspicious!
19.44.3: On thee is laid the Chaturvira Ointment: let all the regions give thee peace and safety. Secure like precious Savitar thou standest: to thee let all these regions bring their tribute. Make one thy salve, thine amulet another, drink one, and with another bathe thy body.
19.44.4: So let the Chaturvira keep us guarded from the four bonds of Nirriti and Grāhi.
19.44.5: May Agni protect me with fire for inspiration and expiration, for strength, for energy, for vigour, for weal and prosperity. All Hail!
19.44.6: May Indra protect me with his Indra-power for inspiration, etc. May Soma protect me with Soma-power, etc.
19.44.7: May Bhaga with good fortune protect me, etc. May the Maruts protect me with their troops for inspiration and expiration, for strength, for energy, for vigour, for weal and prosperity. All Hail!
19.44.8: A charm accompanying investiture with an amulet that ensures safety and victory For manly strength Prajāpati bound thee on first, invincible.
19.44.9: This for long life on thee I bind for splendour, strength, and energy. Invincible, let it guard thee well. Erect, invincible, be this man’s watchful keeper: let not the
19.45.1: Panis or the sorcerers harm thee. 259
19.45.10: Shake off thy foes as Indra scattered Dasyus: quell all enemies. Invincible, let it guard thee well. Indra hath lent the power of sight, and vital breath and strength to this.
19.45.2: Whom even a hundred combatants, striking, have failed to over- come. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
19.45.3: Around thy limbs I place the mail of Indra who hath become the Gods’ imperial Sovran. Again let all the Deities bring thee hither. Invincible let it guard thee well. One and a hundred manly powers, a thousand lives hath this
19.45.4: Amulet, unconquered ever. Go forth a tiger, strike down all thy foemen: let him who would oppose fall low beneath thee.
19.45.5: Invincible, let it guard thee well. Drawn forth from butter, rich in milk and sweetness, hundred- lived, thousand-homed, bestowing vigour,
19.45.6: Kindly, delightsome, full of sap, and mighty, invincible let it guard thee well. That thou mayst be pre-eminent, slayer of rivals, rivalless,
19.45.7: May Savitar cause thee to be chief and controller of thy kin. Invincible, let it guard thee well. A hymn to Night for protection from fiends, robbers, snakes and wolves
19.45.8: Night! the terrestrial realm hath been filled with the Father’s power and might. Thou spreadest forth on high unto the seats of Heaven: dark- ness that strikes with awe comes
19.45.9: near. Each moving thing finds rest in her whose yonder boundary is not seen, nor that which keeps her separate.
19.46.1: O spacious, darksome Night, may we uninjured reach the end of thee, reach, O thou blessed One, thine end.
19.46.2: Thy ninety-nine examiners, O Night, who look upon mankind, Eighty-and-eight in number, or seven-and-seventy are they. Sixty-and-six, O opulent, fifty-and-five, O happy One,
19.46.3: Forty-and-four and thirty-three are they, O thou enriched with spoil. Twenty-and-two hast thou, O Night, eleven, yea, and fewer still.
19.46.4: With these protectors guard us well. O Daughter of the Sky, to- day. Let not a fiends or spiteful man, let no ill-wisher master us. Let not the robber seize our cows, nor the wolf take our sheep today.
19.46.5: Let not the thief, O Blessed, seize our horses, nor she-fiends our men. Let thief and robber run away on pathways most remote from us.
19.46.6: Far from us let Rope with Fangs, far from us let the wicked flee. Do thou make blind and headless. Night, the serpent with his pungent breath. Crush the wolf’s jaws in pieces, strike the robber dead against a post.
19.46.7: In thee, O Night, do we abide: we here will sleep. Be watchful thou. Give thou protection to our kine; and to our horses, and our men.
19.47.1: A hymn to Night for protection Then all that we accumulate, all that the treasure-chest contains,. All this do we entrust to thee.
19.47.2: Entrust thou us to Dawn, O Mother Night. May Dawn entrust us to the Day, and Day to thee, O splendid.
19.47.3: 260 One. Whatever flying thing be here, whatever thing that creeps and. crawls.
19.47.4: Whatever fastens on a joint, therefrom do thou protect us, Night.
19.47.5: So guard thou us from west and east, protect us from the north and south. O splendid One, preserve us: we, the singers of thy praise, are here. They who are followers of Night, and they who watch o’er living things.
19.47.6: They who protect all cattle, they keep watch and ward over our lives, over our herds keep watch and ward.
19.47.7: Verily, Night, I know thy name, Dropper of Fatness art thou called. Thee Bharadvāja knew as such: as such be watchful o’er our wealth. A hymn of Praise and prayer to Night
19.47.8: Friend of the home, the strong and youthful maiden, Night, dear to Savitar the God, and Bhaga,
19.47.9: All-compassing, all-glorious, prompt to listen, hath with her greatness filled the earth and heaven. Over all depths hath she gone up, and mounted, most mighty
19.48.1: One, the sky’s exalted summit. Over me now the loving Night is spreading with her auspicious.
19.48.2: Godlike ways like Mitra. Excellent, high-born, blissful, meet for worship, Night, thou hast come: stay here with friendly spirit.
19.48.3: Guard us, the food for men that we have gotten, and all pro- sperity that comes of cattle. With eager haste hath Night assumed the vigour of leopard,. tiger, or of tawny lion,
19.48.4: The horse’s neighing and the wild-man’s bellow, Thou takest many a form when thou appearest. Kind through the Night be absence of the sunshine: Mother of
19.48.5: Frost, may she be swift to hear us. Take notice of the hymn, thou highly favoured, wherewith I worship thee in all the regions.
19.48.6: Even as a King, O splendid Night, thou takest pleasure in our hymn. May we through Mornings as they flush have all our good men, round us, and become possessors of all wealth.
19.49.1: Yes, Rāmyā is the name thou hast assumed. The men who fain. would spoil. My wealth do thou annoy, O Night, that not one robber may appear, none may a second time
19.49.10: appear. Thou like a well-wrought cup, O Night, art lovely: thou, a. young maid, art formed in perfect beauty.
19.49.2: Thou lovingly, for me with eyes to se: them, hast bound on thee heaven’s stars as thine adornment.
19.49.3: Whatever robber comes to-day, mischievous mortal enemy. Let Night go forth, encounter him, and smite away his neck and head; His feet that he may walk no more, his hands that he may do no harm.
19.49.4: The robber who comes hitherward goes crushed and mutilated hence, Goes hence, goes far away from us, goes hence and bears no spoil away.
19.49.5: A hymn to Night for protection and prosperity 261 Blind him and make him headless, Night! the serpent with the pungent breath.
19.49.6: Strike from his head the wolf’s two eyes, and dash the thief against a post. Those oxen that are thine, O Night, with sharpened horns and rapid pace,
19.49.7: With those transport us safe to-day o’er difficulties everywhere. Uninjured in our bodies may we pass through each succeeding night, And let malignities fail to pass, as men without a boat the depth.
19.49.8: As millet hurried through the air before us is beheld no more. So cause the man to vanish, Night, who plans to do us injury.
19.49.9: The thief hast thou kept far away, the robber driver of our kine. Even him who having covered up the horse’s head would lead him off. If dealing treasure thou hast come to-day, O highly favoured
19.50.1: Night. Cause thou us to enjoy it all so that this may not pass away.
19.50.2: Do thou entrust us to the Dawn, all of us free from sin, O Night. May Dawn deliver us to Day, and Day to thee, O glorious One.
19.50.3: A sacrificial formula Undisturbed am I, undisturbed is my soul, undisturbed mine eye, undisturbed mine ear,
19.50.4: undisturbed is mine in-breathing, undisturbed mine out-breathing, undisturbed my diffusive breath, undisturbed the whole of me. Under the impulse of the God Savitar, sent forth from the arms- of the Asvins and both hands of Pūshan I have taken thee.
19.50.5: A hymn to Kāma or Desire Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire the primal seed and germ of Spirit.
19.50.6: O Kāma dwelling with the lofty Kāma, give growth of riches to the sacrificer. Thou, Kāma, art victorious, famous, potent, splendid, a friend. to him who seeks thy friendship.
19.50.7: Mighty and overpowering in battle, give strength and vigour to the sacrificer. They heard his prayers, and they begot, by Kāma, heavenly- light for him.
19.51.1: Who from a distance longed for it, a dealer ready to exchange. O Kāma, with whatever wish we make this offering to thee, May it be all fulfilled to us. Then taste this sacrifice, All hail!
19.51.2: A hymn to Kāma or Time Prolific, thousand-eyed, and undecaying, a horse with seven reins Time bears us onward.
19.52.1: Sages inspired with holy knowledge mount him: his chariot wheels are all the worlds of creatures. This Time hath seven rolling wheels and seven naves immorality is the chariot’s axle.
19.52.2: This Time brings hitherward all worlds about us: as primal Deity is he entreated.
19.52.3: On Time is laid an overflowing beaker: this we behold in many a place appearing. He carries from us all these worlds of creatures. They call him Kāla in the loftiest heaven.
19.52.4: He only made the worlds of life, he only gathered the worlds of living things together. 262
19.52.5: Their son did he become who was their Father: no other higher power than he existeth. Kāla created yonder heaven, and Kāla made these realms of earth. By Kāla, stirred to motion, both what is and what shall be expand.
19.53.1: Kāla created land; the Sun in Kāla hath his light and heat. In Kāla rest all things that be: in Kāla doth the eye discern.
19.53.10: In Kāla mind, in Kāla breath, in Kāla name are fixt and joined. These living creatures, one and all, rejoice when Kāla hath approached. Kāla embraces Holy Fire, the Highest, Brahma in himself.
19.53.2: Yea, Kāla, who was father of Prajāpati, is Lord of All. He made, he stirred this universe to motion, and on him it rests.
19.53.3: He, Kāla, having now become Brahma, holds Parameshthin up. Kāla created living things and, first of all, Prajāpati. From Kāla self-made Kasyapa, from Kāla Holy Fire was born.
19.53.4: A hymn to Kāla; a continuation of the preceding hymn From Kāla sprang the Waters, sprang the regions, Brahma,
19.53.5: Holy Fire. The Sun ascends by Kāla, and in Kāla sinks again to rest. By Kāla freshly blows the wind, mighty through Kāla is the
19.53.6: Earth: on Kāla rests the mighty Sky. In Kāla erst the text produced what is and what is yet to be.
19.53.7: From Kāla sprang the Richas, and from Kāla was the Yajus born. They formed in Kāla sacrifice, eternal portion for the Gods. In Kāla the Gandharvas and Apsarasas and worlds abide.
19.53.8: Atharvan and this Angiras in Kāla are supreme o’er heaven. Both this world and the world that is most lofty, the pure worlds and pure intermediate
19.53.9: spaces,— Yea, having conquered all the worlds by Brahma, Kāla as God Supreme is supplicated.
19.54.1: A hymn to Agni for protection and prosperity Bringing, as ‘twere, with care unceasing fodder night after night to feed this stabled Courser,
19.54.2: Joying in food and in the growth of riches, may we thy neigh- bours, Agni, ne’er be injured. Here is thine own desire for wealth: through this be gracious unto us. Joying in food and in the growth of riches, may we thy neigh- bours, Agni, ne’er be injured.
19.54.3: Each eve that comes our household’s Lord is Agni, showing his. loving-kindness every morning.
19.54.4: Bestow upon us treasure after treasure: enkindling thee may we increase thy body. Each morn that comes our household’s Lord is Agni, showing. his loving-kindness every evening.
19.54.5: Vouchsafe us treasure after treasure: kindling thee may we prosper through a hundred winters.
19.55.1: Never may I come short of food to feed me. Glory to Agni, Rudra, the consumer and the Lord of food! Protect my company, protect its courteous members, courteous.
19.55.2: God! Only through thee, O much-invoked, may I be ever rich in kine.
19.55.3: 263 Only to thee bringing our tribute, Agni, each day as fodder to a stabled courser, Joying in food and in the growth of riches, may we the neigh- bours, Agni ne’er be injured.
19.55.4: A hymn to Sleep Thou art come hither from the world of Yama: thou, resolute, affectest men with rapture.
19.55.5: Thou, Sleep, created in the Asura’s dwelling, goest, well-know- ing, with the solitary. At first the all-containing, depth beheld thee, ere Night was born, when only Day existed. Thence hast thou come, thence, Sleep, hast thou come hither, concealing, deep within, all
19.55.6: form and figure. Come from the Asuras in lofty, glory, he hath approached the
19.56.1: Gods in search of greatness. Winners of heavenly light, the Three-and-Thirty endowed this Sleep with his supreme dominion.
19.56.2: Of him nor Fathers nor the Gods have knowledge, the Gods whose gentle talk is still about him.
19.56.3: Urged by command of Varuna the Ādityas, Heroes, transported Sleep to Trita Āptya. Thou whose severity hath reached ill-doers, and whose reward the good have gained in
19.56.4: slumber, Delightest heaven with thy most lofty kinship, born from his spirit who was worn and weary.
19.56.5: Of old we know all places whence thou comest. O Sleep, we know him who is here thy ruler. Protect us here illustrious with glory. Go, from afar, with poisons, into distance. A charm against evil dreams
19.56.6: As men discharge the utmost debt, collect the eighth and sixteenth part, So to the foeman we transfer together all the evil dream.
19.57.1: Princes came together, debts came together, Kushthas came to- gether, Sixteenths came together. The whole evil dream that hath visited us we send away as a bad dream to the man who hates us.
19.57.2: Child of Gods’ Consorts, minister of Yama is the good Dream: that which is my trouble we drive away to the enemy.
19.57.3: Thou whose name is Rough art the mouth of the Black Bird. As such we know thee, Dream, as such we know thee well. Like a horse art thou, O Dream. As they bind girth and surcingle on a horse, so bind the alien mischief-maker, the scorner of
19.57.4: the Gods. The evil dream that threatens us, threatens our cattle or our home.
19.57.5: That let the scorner of the Gods, the alien mischief-maker bind as a gold jewel round his neck. Having measured off nine cubits’ distance from us we give away the whole of the evil dream
19.58.1: to the man who hates us. A prayer for prosperity, accompanying a sacrifice
19.58.2: Still equal be the flow of butter ever causing the Year to prosper with oblation. Still be our hearing, sight, and breath uninjured: let us lose nothing of our life and vigour. Let lively breath invite us: we call vital breath to visit us.
19.58.3: Earth and air’s middle realm have gathered, Soma, Brihaspati and Dhartar gathered vigour. 264
19.58.4: The earth and heaven have come to be two gatherers up of vigo- rous might. So let us gather vigour up and closely follow after Earth. With glory come the cows and stand beside the master of the herd. Let us when we have
19.58.5: gathered fame and glory closely follow Earth. Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour wide and
19.58.6: many. Make iron forts defying all assailants: let not your pitcher leak; stay it securely. The eye of sacrifice, source and beginning with voice, car, spirit unto him I offer.
19.59.1: To this our sacrifice, wrought by Visvakarman, may the Gods come gracious and kindly hearted. Let the Gods’ Priests and those who merit worship, to whom oblation as their share is
19.59.2: offered, Come to this holy service with their Consorts, and all Gods revel in the food we bring them. An expiatory hymn accompanying sacrifice
19.59.3: God among mortals, Agni, thou art guard of holy Law, thou art To be adored in sacred rites.
19.60.1: When, ignorant, we violate the statutes of you, O Deities, with whom is knowledge, Wise Agni shall correct our faults and failings, and Soma who hath entered into Brāhmans. To the Gods’ pathway have we come desiring to execute what work we may accomplish.
19.60.2: Let Agni—for he knows—complete the worship. He is the Priest: let him fix rites and seasons.
19.61.1: A prayer for perfect bodily and mental health and vigour May I have voice in my mouth, breath in my nostrils, sight in mine eyes, hearing in mine ears, hair that hath not turned gray, teeth free from yellowness, and much strength in mine
19.62.1: arms. May I have power in my thighs, swiftness in my legs, stedfast- ness in my feet. May all my
19.63.1: members be uninjured and my soul unimpaired. A prayer for long life prosperity and final happiness in heaven May my self remain in my body: may I enjoy the full time of life,
19.64.1: Rest thee pleasantly: pour forth abundance, purifying thyself in Svarga.
19.64.2: A prayer for the love of Gods and men Make me beloved among the Gods, beloved among the Princes, make Me dear to everyone who sees, to Sūdra and to Aryan man.
19.64.3: A prayer, with sacrifice, for long life and prosperity Rise up, O Brāhmanaspati; awake the Gods with sacrifice.
19.64.4: Strengthen the Sacrificer: aid life, breath, and off-spring, cattle, fame. A prayer to Agni for children, long life, and various blessings For lofty Jātavedas I have brought the fuel hither first.
19.65.1: May he who knoweth all bestow faith and intelligence on me. With fuel and with flaming wood we, Jātavedas, strengthen thee;
19.66.1: So do thou strengthen us in turn with children and with store of wealth. Whatever even be the logs which, Agni, we lay down for thee, propitious be it all to me: accept it, O most youthful God.
19.67.1: Agni, these logs are thine: with these be, fain to burn! a flaming brand. Vouchsafe us length of life and give us hope of immortality.
19.67.2: A hymn to Agni identified with the Sun A Golden Eagle thou hast soared with light to heaven. Those who would harm thee as thou fliest skyward.
19.67.3: Beat down, O Jātavedas, with thy fury. The strong hath feared: to heaven mount up with light, O Sūrya.
19.67.4: A hymn to Agni as the Sun The Asuras with iron nets, magicians, who roam about with hooks and bonds of iron, With wrath I make thy thralls, O Jātavedas. Come as a bolt foe- quelling, thousand pointed.
19.67.5: A prayer for long life A hundred autumns may we see.
19.67.6: A hundred autumns may we live. A hundred autumns may we know. A hundred autumns may we grow.
19.67.7: A hundred autumns may we thrive. A hundred autumns may we be.
19.67.8: A hundred autumns may we bide. A hundred, yea, and even more. A preliminary sacrificial formula
19.68.1: Both of broad and narrow I with magic power unclose the mouth. With these when we have raised the bunch of grass we pay the holy rites.
19.69.1: A prayer or charm for long life Ye are alive. I fain would live. I fain would live my complete term of life. Ye live dependent. I fain would live dependent. I fain would live my complete term of life.
19.69.2: Ye remain alive. I fain would remain alive. I fain would live my complete term of life. Ye are life-givers. I fain would live. I fain would live my com- plete term of life.
19.69.3: A charm for long life 266 Live, Indra. Live Sūrya. Live, ye Gods. I fain would live. Fain would I live my complete term
19.69.4: of life. A hymn, accompanying libations, for wealth and prosperity
19.70.1: Let my libations, giving boons, adoring, further the Twice-born’s song that honours Soma. Go ye to Brahma’s world having enriched me with life and breath, with children and with cattle, with fame and wealth, and with a Brāhman’s lustre.
19.71.1: A sacrificial formula Within the chest whence we before extracted the bunch of grass, this do we now deposit.
19.72.1: Wrought is the sacrifice by power of Brahma. Through this assist me here, ye God, with Fervour. 267

20.1.1: The best of guardian hath the man within whose dwelling-place ye drink, O Maruts, giants of the sky.
20.1.2: Let us serve Agni with our hyms, Sage who consumeth ox and cow, Who beareth Soma on his back.
20.1.3: Let the Maruts drink Trishtups from the Potar’s cup, according to the season Soma from heaven.
20.2.1: Let Agni from the Kindler’s cup drink Trishtups, according to the season Soma from heaven. Let Indra the Brāhman from the Brāhman’s cup drink Trishtups, according to the season
20.2.2: Soma from heaven. Let the God, Granter of Wealth, from the Potar’s cup drink
20.2.3: Trishtups, according to the season Soma from heaven. Come, we have pressed the juice for thee: O Indra, drink this
20.2.4: Soma here. Seat thee on this my sacred grass.
20.3: Let both thy bay steeds, yoked by prayer long-maned, O Indra, bring thee nigh. We Soma-bearing Brāhmans call thee Soma-drinker with thy friend,
20.4.1: We, Indra, who have pressed the juice. Like women, let this Soma juice invested with its raiment, glide..
20.4.2: Most active Indra, close to thee. Mighty in bulk, strong-necked, stout-armed in the wild rapture. of the juice
20.4.3: Doth Indra smite the foemen dead. Indra, advance, go forward thou who by thy might art Lord of all.
20.5.1: Slay, Vritra-slayer slay thy foes. Long be thy grasping-hook wherewith thou givest treasure unto- him
20.5.2: Who pours the juice and worships thee. Here, Indra, is thy Soma draught, made pure upon the sacred. grass.
20.5.3: Run hither, come and drink thereof. Famed for thy radiance, worshipped well! this juice is shed for thy delight:
20.5.5: To Kundapāyya, grandson’s son, grandson of Sringavrish, to thee, To him have I addressed my thought.
20.5.6: Indra, with all the Gods promote our wealth-bestowing sacrifice, Thou highly-lauded Lord of men.
20.5.7: Lord of the brave, to thee proceed these drops of Soma juice expressed, The bright drops to thy dwelling-place.
20.6.1: Within thy belly, Indra take Soma the juice most excellent: The heavenly drops belong to thee.
20.6.2: Drink our libation, Lord of hymns: with streams of meath thou art bedewed: Our glory, Indra, is thy gift.
20.6.3: To Indra go the treasures of the worshipper which never fail: He drinks the Soma and is strong.
20.6.4: From far away, from near at hand, O Vritra-slayer, come to us: Accept the songs we sing to thee.
20.6.5: Sūrya, thou mountest up to meet the Hero famous for his wealth, Who hurls the bolt and works for man:
20.6.6: Him who with might of both his arms brake nine-and ninety castles down, Slew Vritra and smote Ahi dead.
20.6.7: This Indra is our gracious Friend. He sends us in a full broad stream Riches in horses, kine, and corn.
20.6.8: Indra, whom many laud, accept the strength-conferring Soma juice. Quaff, pour down drink that satisfies.
20.6.9: Drink as of old, and let the draught delight thee: hear thou my prayer and let our songs exalt thee.
20.7.1: Make the Sun visible, make food abundant: slaughter the foes,. pierce through and free the cattle.
20.7.2: Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover. Here is the pressed juice: drink thereof for rapture.
20.7.3: Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and invocated hear us like a father. Full is his chalice. Blessing! Like a pourer I have filled up the vessel for his drinking.
20.7.4: Presented on the right, dear Soma juices have brought us Indra,. to rejoice him, hither. As cows low to their calves in stalls, so with our songs we glorify
20.8.1: This Indra, even your wondrous God who checks attack, who joys in the delicious juice. Celestial, bounteous Giver, girt about with might, rich, moun- tain-like, in precious things
20.8.2: Him swift we seek for foodful booty rich in kine, brought hundredfold and thousandfold. I crave of thee that hero strength, that thou mayst first regard this prayer,
20.8.3: Wherewith thou helpest Bhrigu and the Yatis and Praskanva when the prize was staked. Wherewith thou sentest mighty waters to the sea, that, Indra, is. thy hero strength.
20.9.1: For ever unattainable is this power of him to whom the worlds. have called aloud. 269
20.9.2: These songs of ours exceeding sweet, these hymns of praise as- cend to thee, Like ever-conquering chariots that display their strength, gain wealth and give unfailing aid.
